@metadata.comment: What each message is, where it shows and what its parameters hold, for translators (banana-i18n's qqq). See packages/i18n/README.md.

app-name: The product's name, shown on the start screen, in the top bar and in the About dialog. Usually not translated.
app-version: Small grey line showing the app's version, on the start screen and in the About dialog. $1: the version number, e.g. "0.19.0".
shell-welcome: Tagline under the app's name on the start screen, the first thing an author sees. A short sentence; keep it warm and calm.
settings-language: Label of the setting, in the Settings dialog (☰ app menu), that picks the language of the app's menus and buttons. It doesn't change the book's own language.
settings-theme: Label of the setting, in the Settings dialog (☰ app menu), that picks light or dark colours. The choices are {{msg-plotdevice|theme-system}}, {{msg-plotdevice|theme-light}} and {{msg-plotdevice|theme-dark}}.
theme-system: Choice under {{msg-plotdevice|settings-theme}} in the Settings dialog: follow the computer's own light or dark setting.
theme-light: Choice under {{msg-plotdevice|settings-theme}} in the Settings dialog: light colours.
theme-dark: Choice under {{msg-plotdevice|settings-theme}} in the Settings dialog: dark colours.
settings-save-failed: Warning at the bottom of the Settings dialog when the settings couldn't be written to disk. The changes still work until the app is closed.
conflict-copy-label: Added in brackets after a chapter's title when the app saves the author's text as a separate copy because the chapter was also changed in another app, e.g. "The Crossing (my version)". Lowercase fragment; it ends up in the copy's title.
dialog-open-project: Title of the system folder picker that opens an existing project (from {{msg-plotdevice|welcome-open-project}}).
dialog-new-project-location: Title of the system folder picker for where a new project's folder will be made (from {{msg-plotdevice|new-project-choose}} on the new-project screen).
dialog-backup-location: Title of the system folder picker for where a backup copy of the book will be saved.
dialog-choose: Confirm button of the system folder pickers. Keep it short: it's a button.
welcome-new-project: Main button on the start screen that begins a new book; it opens the new-project screen. Keep it short: it's a button.
welcome-open-project: Button on the start screen, and item in the ☰ app menu, that shows the folder picker to open an existing project. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
menu-new-project: Item in the ☰ app menu that goes to the new-project screen to start another book. The ellipsis means more choices follow.
welcome-recent: Heading of the list of recently opened projects on the start screen.
welcome-recent-missing: Grey note beside a project in the recent list on the start screen when its folder was moved or deleted. A fragment.
welcome-find: Small button beside a moved or missing project in the start screen's recent list; it shows the folder picker so the author can find it. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
welcome-forget: Small button beside a moved or missing project in the start screen's recent list; it takes the project off the list without deleting anything.
welcome-bring-in-question: Question at the bottom of the start screen, followed by the link {{msg-plotdevice|welcome-bring-in}} to a guide about moving existing notes or drafts into Plot Device.
welcome-bring-in: Link after {{msg-plotdevice|welcome-bring-in-question}} on the start screen; it opens the online guide to moving existing notes and drafts into the app. The arrow points forward; flip it for right-to-left languages if needed.
new-project-title-label: Label of the field for the new book's title, on the new-project screen.
new-project-author-label: Label of the field for the author's name as it should appear on the book's cover, on the new-project screen. The field may be left empty.
new-project-language-label: Label of the drop-down that sets the language the book is written in, on the new-project screen. This is the book's language, not the app's.
new-project-create: Button that creates the new book, at the bottom of the new-project screen. Keep it short: it's a button.
new-project-hint: Grey note near the bottom of the new-project screen: the outlines and page names the template creates use the book's language (chosen with {{msg-plotdevice|new-project-language-label}}), not the app's.
new-project-question: Big heading of the new-project screen, above the cards for the kinds of project (Novel, Short story and so on). A question to the author.
new-project-adjust-later: Grey line under {{msg-plotdevice|new-project-question}} on the new-project screen, reassuring the author that the choice isn't final. "Kinds of pages" means characters, places, notes and the book's own kinds.
new-project-back: Link at the top of the new-project screen that goes back to the start screen. The arrow points back; flip it for right-to-left languages if needed.
new-project-templates: Screen-reader-only name of the group of project-kind cards (Novel, Short story, D&D campaign, Blank) on the new-project screen.
new-project-location-label: Label of the folder where the new book will be kept, on the new-project screen; the folder path is shown beside it with {{msg-plotdevice|new-project-choose}}.
new-project-choose: Button beside the folder path on the new-project screen; it shows the folder picker to choose another place. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
template-novel: Name of the Novel template, the big title on one of the project-kind cards on the new-project screen (after {{msg-plotdevice|welcome-new-project}} on the start screen). Keep it short.
template-novel-description: One-sentence description on the Novel card on the new-project screen, under its name. A full sentence.
template-novel-kinds: Preview line on the Novel card on the new-project screen: the kinds of pages this template creates, separated by " · ". Use the same words as the kind names elsewhere in the app. Hidden from screen readers.
template-novel-outlines: Preview line on the Novel card on the new-project screen: the names of the outlines this template creates, separated by " · ". Hidden from screen readers. "Main story" is a three-act plan; "Loose ideas" is a place for unsorted ideas.
template-novel-summary: Small grey line at the bottom of the Novel card on the new-project screen, counting what the template creates. A fragment, not a sentence; keep the " · " separators.
template-short-story: Name of the Short story template, the big title on one of the project-kind cards on the new-project screen (after {{msg-plotdevice|welcome-new-project}} on the start screen). Keep it short.
template-short-story-description: One-sentence description on the Short story card on the new-project screen, under its name. A full sentence.
template-short-story-kinds: Preview line on the Short story card on the new-project screen: the kinds of pages this template creates, separated by " · ". Use the same words as the kind names elsewhere in the app. Hidden from screen readers.
template-short-story-outlines: Preview line on the Short story card on the new-project screen: the name of the one outline this template creates, followed by its three sections. Hidden from screen readers.
template-short-story-summary: Small grey line at the bottom of the Short story card on the new-project screen, counting what the template creates. A fragment, not a sentence; keep the " · " separators.
template-poetry: Name of the Poetry collection template, the big title on one of the project-kind cards on the new-project screen (after {{msg-plotdevice|welcome-new-project}} on the start screen). Keep it short. Hebrew: „ספר שירה”, approved by the owner (ADR 0013).
template-poetry-description: One-sentence description on the Poetry collection card on the new-project screen, under its name. A full sentence.
template-poetry-kinds: Preview line on the Poetry collection card on the new-project screen: the kinds of pages this template creates (only Notes). Use the same word as the Notes kind elsewhere in the app. Hidden from screen readers.
template-poetry-outlines: Preview line on the Poetry collection card on the new-project screen: the name of the outline this template creates, and what it holds. „אסופה” is the book's word for a group of poems (ADR 0013). Hidden from screen readers.
template-poetry-summary: Small grey line at the bottom of the Poetry collection card on the new-project screen, counting what the template creates; "poems" says chapters are called poems. A fragment, not a sentence; keep the " · " separators.
template-campaign: Name of the D&D campaign (a tabletop role-playing game campaign) template, the big title on one of the project-kind cards on the new-project screen (after {{msg-plotdevice|welcome-new-project}} on the start screen). "D&D" is Dungeons & Dragons; usually not translated. Keep it short.
template-campaign-description: One-sentence description on the D&D campaign card on the new-project screen, under its name. A full sentence. "Sessions" are game sessions, which replace chapters in this kind of project; NPCs are non-player characters (keep the common gaming term in your language).
template-campaign-kinds: Preview line on the D&D campaign card on the new-project screen: the kinds of pages this template creates, separated by " · ". Use the same words as the kind names elsewhere in the app. Hidden from screen readers. NPCs are non-player characters; use the usual gaming term.
template-campaign-outlines: Preview line on the D&D campaign card on the new-project screen: the names of the outlines this template creates, separated by " · ". Hidden from screen readers. A plan for one game session, and a plan for the whole campaign's story.
template-campaign-summary: Small grey line at the bottom of the D&D campaign card on the new-project screen, counting what the template creates. "sessions" means the project has game sessions instead of chapters. A fragment, not a sentence; keep the " · " separators.
template-blank: Name of the Blank (empty) template, the big title on one of the project-kind cards on the new-project screen (after {{msg-plotdevice|welcome-new-project}} on the start screen). Keep it short.
template-blank-description: One-sentence description on the Blank card on the new-project screen, under its name. A full sentence.
template-blank-kinds: Preview line on the Blank card on the new-project screen: the kinds of pages this template creates, separated by " · ". Use the same words as the kind names elsewhere in the app. Hidden from screen readers.
template-blank-summary: Small grey line at the bottom of the Blank card on the new-project screen, counting what the template creates. It creates no outlines. A fragment, not a sentence; keep the " · " separators.
open-failed-not-a-project: Error notice when the author opens a folder that isn't a Plot Device project, shown on the start screen. Don't translate the file name `project.md`.
open-failed-unreadable: Error notice when a project's files couldn't be read while opening it. Shown on the start screen.
open-failed-newer-format: Error notice when a project was saved by a newer version of the app and this version can't open it. Shown on the start screen; the author should update the app.
open-failed-not-recent: Error notice when the author picks a project from the start screen's recent list that has since been removed from it.
create-failed-folder-exists: Error notice on the new-project screen when a folder with the new book's name already exists in the chosen place.
create-failed-inside-project: Error notice on the new-project screen when the chosen place is inside another book's folder.
create-failed: Error notice on the new-project screen when a new book couldn't be created for any other reason.
sidebar-toggle: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the icon button at the top of a chapter or page that shows or hides the sidebar. The tooltip adds the keyboard shortcut in brackets after it.
navigator-label: Default plural word for the book's chapters: the screen-reader name of the chapter list in the Write sidebar, and a group heading in the link picker. A book may replace it with its own word, e.g. "Sessions".
chapter-number: A chapter's number, shown above its title on the page and in the Write workspace. $1: the chapter's position in the book, e.g. 3. A book may use its own word instead, e.g. "Session 3".
navigator-new-chapter: Link under the chapter list in the Write sidebar, and the button on the empty Write page, that adds a new chapter and opens it. The site's guide shows it with "+ " in front. Keep it short.
navigator-new-unit: Replaces {{msg-plotdevice|navigator-new-chapter}} when the book calls its chapters something else. $1: the book's own word for one chapter, e.g. "Session", in the book's language. Keep it short.
write-empty-unit-text: Text on the empty Write page when the book has no chapters yet and calls its chapters by its own word, e.g. "Session". Replaces {{msg-plotdevice|write-empty-text}}; "it" is the first chapter (session) to be made.
navigator-new-part: Link under the chapter list in the Write sidebar that adds a new part (a group of chapters) at the end of the book. The site's guide shows it with "+ " in front. Keep it short.
navigator-not-in-book: Heading in the Write sidebar for chapters that are kept but taken out of the book's reading order (not exported); also shown above such a chapter's title. Chapters get here through {{msg-plotdevice|chapter-remove}}. A short phrase meaning "set aside, not in the book".
navigator-missing: Heading in the Write sidebar for chapters listed in the book whose files were moved or deleted outside the app.
navigator-add-to-book: Small button beside a chapter under {{msg-plotdevice|navigator-not-in-book}} in the Write sidebar; it puts the chapter back into the book's reading order.
navigator-relink: Small button beside a missing chapter in the Write sidebar, offering a file the app found that is probably the same chapter. $1: that file's name, e.g. "crossing.md" (not translated).
navigator-update-title: Small button under a chapter in the Write sidebar when the chapter's title changed but the book's contents still show the old name. $1: the chapter's new title, e.g. "The Crossing".
navigator-no-chapters: Grey line in the Write sidebar when the book has no chapters yet.
write-empty-title: Heading on the empty Write page when the book has no chapters yet.
write-empty-text: Text under {{msg-plotdevice|write-empty-title}} on the empty Write page, above the button that starts the first chapter. Full sentences.
chapter-actions: Screen-reader label of a chapter's ⋯ menu button, in the Write sidebar and above the chapter's page. $1: the chapter's title, e.g. "The Crossing".
chapter-rename: Item in a chapter's ⋯ menu that changes the chapter's title. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
chapter-rename-file: Item in a chapter's ⋯ menu that changes the name of the chapter's file on disk (not its title). The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
chapter-move-up: Item in a chapter's ⋯ menu that moves the chapter one place earlier in the book.
chapter-move-down: Item in a chapter's ⋯ menu that moves the chapter one place later in the book.
chapter-move-to: Start of items in a chapter's ⋯ menu that move the chapter to a place; the code adds ": " and the place, e.g. {{msg-plotdevice|move-to-start}} or {{msg-plotdevice|move-to-part}}.
move-to-start: Place in a chapter's ⋯ menu, after {{msg-plotdevice|chapter-move-to}} and ": ": the very beginning of the book. A fragment.
move-to-end: Place in a chapter's ⋯ menu, after {{msg-plotdevice|chapter-move-to}} and ": ": the very end of the book. A fragment.
move-to-part: Place in a chapter's ⋯ menu, after {{msg-plotdevice|chapter-move-to}} and ": ": the end of a part. $1: the part's name, e.g. "Part One". A fragment.
chapter-remove: Item in a chapter's ⋯ menu that takes the chapter out of the book's reading order without deleting it; it then waits under {{msg-plotdevice|navigator-not-in-book}}.
part-actions: Screen-reader label of a part's ⋯ menu button in the Write sidebar. $1: the part's name, e.g. "Part One".
part-rename: Item in a part's ⋯ menu in the Write sidebar that renames the part. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
part-rename-unit: Item in a part's ⋯ menu in the sidebar, in a book that has its own word for parts (ADR 0013), such as a poetry collection's sections. $1 is that word, singular, as the author wrote it ("Section", „אסופה”). Like {{msg-plotdevice|part-rename}}.
prompt-chapter-title: Label in the small dialog that asks for a chapter's title, when adding or renaming a chapter.
prompt-poem-title: Label of the text box when adding or renaming a poem (a chapter that is a poem, ADR 0013). The title may be left empty: the poem is then known by its first line.
prompt-part-name: Label in the small dialog that asks for a part's name, when adding or renaming a part.
prompt-part-unit-name: Label of the text box when adding or renaming a part, in a book that has its own word for parts (ADR 0013). $1 is that word, singular, as the author wrote it ("Section", „אסופה”). Like {{msg-plotdevice|prompt-part-name}}.
prompt-file-name: Label in the small dialog that asks for a chapter's new file name, from {{msg-plotdevice|chapter-rename-file}}.
prompt-link: Label in the small dialog that asks for a web address, when adding or editing a link in the text.
prompt-ok: Confirm button of the small dialogs that ask for a title, name or link. Keep it short: it's a button.
prompt-cancel: Button that closes a dialog without changing anything, used in many dialogs; also the screen-reader label of the × that dismisses a notice. Keep it short: it's a button.
change-failed-stale: Error notice when a change to the book's contents (adding, moving or renaming a chapter or part) couldn't be made because the contents were changed in another app at the same time.
change-failed-name-taken: Error notice when renaming a file, such as a chapter's file, to a name another file already has.
change-failed-invalid-name: Error notice when the new name for a file contains characters a file name can't have.
change-failed: Error notice when a change to the book (adding, moving or renaming something) failed for any other reason.
chapter-text: Screen-reader name of the writing area where the chapter's text is typed, in the Write workspace.
chapter-form-poem: Small label beside the chapter's number above the page, when a chapter is a poem in a book whose new chapters are prose (ADR 0013). One word.
chapter-form-prose: Small label beside the chapter's number above the page, when a chapter is prose in a book whose new chapters are poems, such as a poetry collection (ADR 0013). One word.
chapter-title-field: Name read out by screen readers for the chapter's title above the page, which the author can click and retype (Milestone 28). One word: what the field is.
poem-untitled: Shown in italics above the page for a poem with no title (ADR 0013), and in the sidebar while it has no text yet; once it has text, the sidebar shows its first line instead. Shown in the book's language, not the interface's, because it stands where the poem's title would be.
scene-break: Screen-reader name of the ⁂ mark in the text that separates two scenes inside a chapter.
chapter-unreadable: Warning above a chapter or page when its file can't be shown because it isn't valid text or its details (the information at the top of the file) are damaged. Also used for pages and outlines, not only chapters.
chapter-missing: Warning shown instead of a chapter or page when its file is missing from the book's folder.
save-saved: Save status in the top bar: everything is saved to disk. Keep it short.
save-saving: Save status in the top bar while the text is being written to disk. Keep it short.
save-unsaved: Save status in the top bar right after typing, before the automatic save. Keep it short.
save-conflict: Save status in the top bar when the open chapter was changed by another app; nothing was overwritten. Keep it short.
save-failed: Save status in the top bar when saving failed; the text stays in the app and saving is tried again. Full sentences.
toolbar-format: Menu button at the top corner of the page with every formatting command; also the screen-reader name of the small formatting bubble that appears over selected text. Keep it short.
format-more: Screen-reader label and tooltip of the ⋯ button in the formatting bubble over selected text; it opens the other formatting commands.
format-bold: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the bold button in the formatting bubble over selected text, and a formatting menu item.
format-italic: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the italic button in the formatting bubble over selected text, and a formatting menu item.
format-heading1: Formatting menu item that turns the current paragraph into a top-level heading (as in Word or Google Docs). The keyboard shortcut is shown beside it.
format-heading2: Formatting command that makes the current paragraph a medium-size heading. Item in the Format menu at the corner of a chapter, an outline's text or a page, and in the ⋯ menu of the bubble that appears over selected text. Its keyboard shortcut is shown beside it. Keep it short.
format-heading3: Formatting command that makes the current paragraph a small heading. Item in the Format menu at the corner of a chapter, an outline's text or a page, and in the ⋯ menu of the bubble that appears over selected text. Its keyboard shortcut is shown beside it. Keep it short.
format-body: Formatting command that turns a heading back into ordinary paragraph text. Item in the Format menu at the corner of a chapter, an outline's text or a page, and in the ⋯ menu of the bubble that appears over selected text. Keep it short.
format-quote: Formatting command that makes the current paragraph a block quotation. Item in the Format menu at the corner of a chapter, an outline's text or a page, and the tooltip and screen-reader label of the quote button in the bubble over selected text. Keep it short.
format-bulletList: Formatting command that makes the current paragraph an item of a list with bullet points. Item in the Format menu at the corner of a chapter, an outline's text or a page. Keep it short.
format-orderedList: Formatting command that makes the current paragraph an item of a numbered list (1, 2, 3). Item in the Format menu at the corner of a chapter, an outline's text or a page. Keep it short.
format-sceneBreak: Formatting command that inserts a scene break, the small divider between scenes within a chapter. Item in the Format menu at the corner of a chapter, an outline's text or a page.
format-poem: Checked item in the Format menu of a chapter: on when the chapter is a poem (ADR 0013). A poem keeps its lines: Enter starts a new line and Enter twice a new stanza. Switching it never changes the words. One word.
niqqud-menu: Item in the Format menu: opens the niqqud picker, a small panel for adding Hebrew vowel marks to the letter before the cursor (ADR 0013). Keep the word niqqud (Hebrew vowel points); ends with an ellipsis because it opens a panel.
niqqud-title: Name of the niqqud picker panel, announced by screen readers when it opens (ADR 0013).
niqqud-hint: Small grey line at the bottom of the niqqud picker. The arrow keys move to the next or previous Hebrew letter.
niqqud-no-letter: Shown in the niqqud picker when the cursor isn't right after a Hebrew letter, so there is nothing to add marks to.
niqqud-qamats: Name of a Hebrew vowel mark (U+05B8), the label of its button in the niqqud picker, read by screen readers and shown on hover.
niqqud-patah: Name of a Hebrew vowel mark (U+05B7), the label of its button in the niqqud picker.
niqqud-tsere: Name of a Hebrew vowel mark (U+05B5), the label of its button in the niqqud picker.
niqqud-segol: Name of a Hebrew vowel mark (U+05B6), the label of its button in the niqqud picker.
niqqud-hiriq: Name of a Hebrew vowel mark (U+05B4), the label of its button in the niqqud picker.
niqqud-holam: Name of a Hebrew vowel mark (U+05B9), the label of its button in the niqqud picker.
niqqud-qubuts: Name of a Hebrew vowel mark (U+05BB), the label of its button in the niqqud picker.
niqqud-sheva: Name of a Hebrew vowel mark (U+05B0), the label of its button in the niqqud picker.
niqqud-hataf-patah: Name of a Hebrew vowel mark (U+05B2), the label of its button in the niqqud picker.
niqqud-hataf-segol: Name of a Hebrew vowel mark (U+05B1), the label of its button in the niqqud picker.
niqqud-hataf-qamats: Name of a Hebrew vowel mark (U+05B3), the label of its button in the niqqud picker.
niqqud-dagesh: Name of a Hebrew mark, the dot inside a letter (U+05BC), the label of its button in the niqqud picker.
niqqud-shin-dot: Name of the dot on the right of the letter shin (U+05C1), the label of its button in the niqqud picker.
niqqud-sin-dot: Name of the dot on the left of the letter shin, making it sin (U+05C2), the label of its button in the niqqud picker.
format-link: Command that adds a link from the selected text to a chapter, page or web address. Item in the Format menu at the corner of a chapter, an outline's text or a page, and the tooltip and screen-reader label of the link button in the bubble over selected text. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
toolbar-link: Screen-reader-only label (aria-label) of the small bubble that appears when the cursor is on a link in the text; the bubble holds {{msg-plotdevice|link-open}}, {{msg-plotdevice|link-change}} and {{msg-plotdevice|link-remove}}. A noun: "link".
link-goes-to: Text at the start of the bubble that appears when the cursor is on a link, saying where the link leads. $1: the name of the chapter or page it links to, or a web address, e.g. "Mara Venn".
link-open: Button in the bubble over a link in the text; opens the chapter, page or web address the link leads to. Keep it short: it's a button.
link-change: Button in the bubble over a link in the text; lets the author choose a different place for the link to lead to (the linked words stay the same). The ellipsis means a dialog follows. Keep it short: it's a button.
link-remove: Button in the bubble over a link in the text; removes the link but keeps its words. Keep it short: it's a button.
plain-text-edit: Menu item that switches a chapter, an outline's text or a page to plain text, showing every formatting mark (such as # for headings) so the author can fix something by hand. Appears in the Format menu at the page's corner and in the Story workspace's outline menu.
plain-text-banner: Notice shown across the top of a chapter, outline or page while it is in plain-text view, where formatting marks are shown and edited as typed characters. Followed by the button {{msg-plotdevice|plain-text-back}}. A full sentence.
plain-text-back: Button in the plain-text notice, and menu item in the Format menu, that returns from plain text (all formatting marks visible) to the normal, formatted view. Replaces {{msg-plotdevice|plain-text-edit}} in the menu while plain text is on.
plain-text-switch: Toggle button beside {{msg-plotdevice|toolbar-format}} at the page's corner, shown only when {{msg-plotdevice|settings-plain-text-switch}} is on. Pressed while the chapter, page or outline text shows plain text (every formatting mark visible). Keep it short: it's a small button.
direction-paragraph-ltr: Item in the Format menu of a chapter in the Write workspace: makes the current paragraph run left to right (as in English), whatever the book's own direction. For mixing languages such as Hebrew and English.
direction-paragraph-rtl: Item in the Format menu of a chapter in the Write workspace: makes the current paragraph run right to left (as in Hebrew), whatever the book's own direction.
direction-paragraph-clear: Item in the Format menu of a chapter in the Write workspace: removes a paragraph's own direction so it follows the book's direction again (left to right or right to left). "Like the book" means "in the book's direction".
direction-phrase-ltr: Item in the Format menu of a chapter in the Write workspace: makes only the selected words, inside a paragraph, run left to right (as in English).
direction-phrase-rtl: Item in the Format menu of a chapter in the Write workspace: makes only the selected words, inside a paragraph, run right to left (as in Hebrew).
direction-phrase-clear: Item in the Format menu of a chapter in the Write workspace: removes the selected words' own direction so they follow their paragraph's direction again.
focus-enter: Button in the Page appearance panel (the "Aa" button) that turns on focus mode, which hides everything around the chapter so only the writing shows. Its keyboard shortcut is shown beside it. Keep it short.
focus-exit: Button at the top of a chapter in the Write workspace while focus mode is on; turns focus mode off and brings back the rest of the window. Keep it short: it's a button.
conflict-title: Title of the dialog that appears when the open chapter's file was changed by another program (for example a sync service or another editor) while the author was writing in Plot Device.
conflict-body: Explanation in the dialog titled {{msg-plotdevice|conflict-title}}. $1: the chapter's title, e.g. "The Crossing". "Plot Device" is the product name: usually not translated. The author's latest text is safe but has not yet been saved over the other version.
conflict-keep-both: Main button in the dialog titled {{msg-plotdevice|conflict-title}}; keeps both the author's text and the other version. Explained by {{msg-plotdevice|conflict-keep-both-detail}} below it. Keep it short: it's a button.
conflict-keep-both-detail: Explanation below the button {{msg-plotdevice|conflict-keep-both}} in the dialog about a chapter changed in another app. A full sentence.
conflict-use-mine: Button in the dialog titled {{msg-plotdevice|conflict-title}}; saves the author's text over the version changed in the other app. Explained by the warning {{msg-plotdevice|conflict-use-mine-detail}} below it. Keep it short: it's a button.
conflict-use-mine-detail: Warning below the button {{msg-plotdevice|conflict-use-mine}} in the dialog about a chapter changed in another app. A full sentence.
conflict-kept: Short notice after the author chose {{msg-plotdevice|conflict-keep-both}} for a chapter: their text became a new chapter. $1: the new chapter's title. "On the side" is the name of the list of chapters that are not part of the book; use the same words as {{msg-plotdevice|navigator-not-in-book}}.
conflict-kept-beside: Short notice after the author chose {{msg-plotdevice|conflict-keep-both}} for a file that isn't a chapter, such as a page or an outline: their text was saved as a new file next to it. $1: the new file's name.
conflict-failed: Error notice when saving the author's choice in the dialog about a chapter changed in another app didn't work. Reassures that their text is still safe. Full sentences.
settings: Heading of the Settings dialog, which holds the app's preferences (such as the interface language).
settings-open: Item in the ☰ app menu that opens the Settings dialog. The ellipsis means a dialog follows. Its keyboard shortcut is shown beside it.
menu-view: Name of the View menu in the native menu bar at the top of the window or screen (zoom, full screen and similar). Use the usual word for this menu in the operating system's language.
app-menu: Screen-reader label (aria-label) and tooltip of the ☰ button at the top corner of the window, which opens the app menu (new project, open, settings, help).
book-menu: Screen-reader label (aria-label) and tooltip of the button showing the book's title at the top of the window, which opens the book menu (Export, kinds of pages, a chapter's versions).
appearance: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the "Aa" button at the top of a chapter or page, which opens a small panel for text size, page width and focus mode. Also the panel's name. Refers to how the writing page looks, not the whole app.
settings-writing-size: Label in the Page appearance panel (the "Aa" button) for the choice of how large the writing text is; followed by three buttons {{msg-plotdevice|size-small}}, {{msg-plotdevice|size-medium}}, {{msg-plotdevice|size-large}}.
size-small: Tooltip and screen-reader label of one of three "A" buttons for {{msg-plotdevice|settings-writing-size}} in the Page appearance panel: small text. An adjective describing the text size.
size-medium: Tooltip and screen-reader label of one of three "A" buttons for {{msg-plotdevice|settings-writing-size}} in the Page appearance panel: medium-size text. An adjective describing the text size.
size-large: Tooltip and screen-reader label of one of three "A" buttons for {{msg-plotdevice|settings-writing-size}} in the Page appearance panel: large text. An adjective describing the text size.
settings-page-width: Label in the Page appearance panel (the "Aa" button) for the choice of how wide the column of writing is; followed by three buttons {{msg-plotdevice|width-narrow}}, {{msg-plotdevice|width-medium}}, {{msg-plotdevice|width-wide}}.
width-narrow: One of three buttons for {{msg-plotdevice|settings-page-width}} in the Page appearance panel. An adjective describing the page width. Keep it short: it's a button.
width-medium: One of three buttons for {{msg-plotdevice|settings-page-width}} in the Page appearance panel; a middle width. An adjective describing the page width (may need a different form from {{msg-plotdevice|size-medium}}). Keep it short: it's a button.
width-wide: One of three buttons for {{msg-plotdevice|settings-page-width}} in the Page appearance panel. An adjective describing the page width. Keep it short: it's a button.
spelling-add: Item in the right-click menu on a word the spellchecker marked as misspelled; adds the word to the dictionary so it's no longer marked.
edit-cut: Item in the right-click menu in text: Cut. Use the usual word from the operating system's own menus.
edit-copy: Item in the right-click menu in text: Copy. Use the usual word from the operating system's own menus.
edit-paste: Item in the right-click menu in text: Paste. Use the usual word from the operating system's own menus.
workspace-switch: Screen-reader-only label (aria-label) of the pair of buttons at the top of the window that switch between the two workspaces, {{msg-plotdevice|workspace-story}} and {{msg-plotdevice|workspace-write}}.
workspace-story: Button at the top of the window that switches to the Story workspace, the story's planning space (outlines, characters, places and other pages); also the screen-reader label of that workspace's sidebar. "Story" is a working name that may change: translate the meaning if that reads better. Keep it short: it's a button.
workspace-write: Button at the top of the window that switches to the Write workspace, where the author writes the chapters. Keep it short: it's a button; a verb, "to write".
story-plot: Heading of the group in the Story workspace's sidebar that lists the outlines (the plans of the story). It can be folded. A noun: the plot.
story-world: Heading of the group in the Story workspace's sidebar that lists the kinds of pages about the story's world: characters, places, notes and the book's own kinds. It can be folded.
story-new-outline: Button that creates a new outline (a plan of sections and cards). Shown under the outlines in the Story workspace's sidebar and on the empty Story workspace when there's no outline yet.
start-writing: Faint hint shown inside an empty chapter, page or outline text, where the author starts typing. Disappears once they type. A short sentence. Shown in the book's language, not the interface's.
story-empty-title: Title shown in the Story workspace when the book has no outline yet; followed by {{msg-plotdevice|story-empty-text}} and the button {{msg-plotdevice|story-new-outline}}.
story-empty-text: Explanation shown in the Story workspace when the book has no outline yet, below {{msg-plotdevice|story-empty-title}}. "Sections" and "cards" are the app's names for the parts of an outline: a section is a big step, shown as a column; a card is a moment within it. Full sentences.
gallery-empty-character: Title shown in the Story workspace when the book has no character pages yet; followed by {{msg-plotdevice|gallery-empty-character-text}} and a button to add one.
gallery-empty-character-text: Explanation shown when the book has no character pages yet, below {{msg-plotdevice|gallery-empty-character}}. "Other names" means nicknames and aliases. A full sentence.
gallery-empty-place: Title shown in the Story workspace when the book has no place pages yet; followed by {{msg-plotdevice|gallery-empty-place-text}} and a button to add one.
gallery-empty-place-text: Explanation shown when the book has no place pages yet, below {{msg-plotdevice|gallery-empty-place}}. A full sentence.
gallery-empty-note: Title shown in the Story workspace when the book has no note pages yet; followed by {{msg-plotdevice|gallery-empty-note-text}} and a button to add one.
gallery-empty-note-text: Explanation shown when the book has no note pages yet, below {{msg-plotdevice|gallery-empty-note}}. Notes are pages about the story's world that aren't characters or places. A full sentence.
new-page-of-kind: Button on the empty Story-workspace list of one of the book's own kinds of pages; adds a new page of that kind. $1: the kind's name in the singular, as the author typed it, e.g. "Faction". Since $1 can be any word in any language, phrase it so no adjective has to agree with it (Hebrew uses "Adding $1").
gallery-empty-kind: Title shown when there are no pages yet of one of the book's own kinds, or no chapters when the book calls its chapters something else. $1: the kind's plural name as the author typed it, e.g. "Factions" or "Sessions". Phrase it so nothing has to agree with $1 in gender.
gallery-empty-kind-text: Explanation shown when there are no pages yet of one of the book's own kinds (such as Factions), below {{msg-plotdevice|gallery-empty-kind}}. "Other names" means nicknames and aliases. A full sentence.
tag-all-kind: Heading of the folded group at the end of a list of pages grouped by tags, holding the pages without any of the chosen tags. $1: the plural name of one of the book's own kinds, e.g. "Factions"; $2: how many pages are in the group.
story-unsorted: Heading in the Story workspace's sidebar, and in the Kinds of pages dialog, over folders of pages that the book doesn't list as a kind of page. Nothing is lost; each such folder can be made a kind.
kinds-menu: Item in the book menu (opened from the book's title at the top) that opens the Kinds of pages dialog, where the author adds, renames and orders kinds of pages such as Characters or Factions. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
new-chapters-poems: Checked item in the book menu (the book's name at the top): when on, every new chapter starts as a poem (ADR 0013). On in a poetry collection. Existing chapters don't change.
kinds-title: Title of the dialog where the author manages the book's kinds of pages (Characters, Places, Notes, and their own such as Factions).
kinds-hint: Explanation at the top of the Kinds of pages dialog. "Plot Device" is the product name: usually not translated. A kind's pages are kept in a folder of the book on disk. Full sentences.
kinds-actions: Screen-reader label (aria-label) and tooltip of the ⋯ menu button beside each kind in the Kinds of pages dialog. $1: the kind's plural name, e.g. "Factions".
kinds-rename: Item in the ⋯ menu beside a kind in the Kinds of pages dialog; lets the author change the kind's name. The ellipsis means more input follows.
kinds-move-up: Item in the ⋯ menu beside a kind in the Kinds of pages dialog; moves the kind one place up in the list (the order used in the Story workspace's sidebar).
kinds-move-down: Item in the ⋯ menu beside a kind in the Kinds of pages dialog; moves the kind one place down in the list.
kinds-remove: Item in the ⋯ menu beside a kind in the Kinds of pages dialog; removes the kind from the list (its pages are kept). The ellipsis means a confirmation follows.
kinds-remove-confirm: Confirmation question before removing a kind of page in the Kinds of pages dialog. $1: the kind's plural name, e.g. "Factions"; $2: how many pages of that kind exist. "Not sorted yet" refers to {{msg-plotdevice|story-unsorted}}; use the same words. Confirmed with {{msg-plotdevice|kinds-remove-action}}.
kinds-remove-action: Confirmation button in the question {{msg-plotdevice|kinds-remove-confirm}}. Keep it short: it's a button.
kinds-add: Button at the end of the list in the Kinds of pages dialog; opens fields to add a new kind of page, such as Factions.
kinds-adopt: Button beside a folder of pages that isn't a kind yet, in the Kinds of pages dialog and at the top of that folder's list in the Story workspace; turns the folder into a kind of page. The ellipsis means more input follows.
kinds-field-one: Label of the field for a kind of page's name in the singular, e.g. "Faction", in the Kinds of pages dialog; also for the singular of what the book calls a chapter. Paired with {{msg-plotdevice|kinds-field-many}}.
kinds-field-many: Label of the field for a kind of page's name in the plural, e.g. "Factions", in the Kinds of pages dialog; also for the plural of what the book calls a chapter. A noun: the plural form.
kinds-field-folder: Label of the field for the name of the folder on disk where a new kind's pages are kept, in the Kinds of pages dialog.
kinds-one-placeholder: Example shown faintly in the empty singular-name field in the Kinds of pages dialog: a group in the story's world, such as a political faction. Translate as a natural example in the singular, matching {{msg-plotdevice|kinds-many-placeholder}}.
kinds-many-placeholder: Example shown faintly in the empty plural-name field in the Kinds of pages dialog. The plural of {{msg-plotdevice|kinds-one-placeholder}}.
kinds-folder-stays: Note shown while renaming a kind in the Kinds of pages dialog, saying its folder on disk keeps its name. $1: the folder's name with a slash, e.g. "factions/"; not translated. A full sentence.
kinds-save: Button that saves a kind of page's names, or what the book calls its chapters, in the Kinds of pages dialog. Keep it short: it's a button.
kinds-not-saved: Error shown in the Kinds of pages dialog when a kind can't be saved: the singular and plural names are both required, and the folder name must not exist yet and must be valid on Windows, Mac and Linux. A full sentence.
kinds-unit-title: Heading of the part of the Kinds of pages dialog where the author can rename what the book calls a chapter, e.g. "Session" for a role-playing campaign.
kinds-unit-hint: Explanation under {{msg-plotdevice|kinds-unit-title}} in the Kinds of pages dialog. "Plot Device" is the product name: usually not translated. Quote "chapter" in the same word the app uses for a chapter. Full sentences.
kinds-unit-one-placeholder: Shown faintly in the empty singular field for what the book calls a chapter; the default word, in the singular. Use the app's own word for "chapter".
kinds-unit-many-placeholder: Shown faintly in the empty plural field for what the book calls a chapter; the default word, in the plural. Use the app's own word for "chapters".
kinds-part-unit-title: Heading on the "Kinds of pages" screen, above two boxes for the book's own word for a part, such as "Section" in a poetry collection (ADR 0013). Like {{msg-plotdevice|kinds-unit-title}}.
kinds-part-unit-hint: Grey line under {{msg-plotdevice|kinds-part-unit-title}} on the "Kinds of pages" screen. Like {{msg-plotdevice|kinds-unit-hint}}.
kinds-part-unit-one-placeholder: Placeholder in the box for the singular word for a part, under {{msg-plotdevice|kinds-part-unit-title}}.
kinds-part-unit-many-placeholder: Placeholder in the box for the plural word for parts, under {{msg-plotdevice|kinds-part-unit-title}}.
kinds-close: Button that closes the Kinds of pages dialog. Keep it short: it's a button.
kinds-mismatch: Note in the Kinds of pages dialog when some kinds were renamed but their folders on disk still have the old names; followed by the button {{msg-plotdevice|kinds-match-folders}}. Full sentences.
kinds-match-folders: Button in the Kinds of pages dialog that opens the dialog {{msg-plotdevice|match-title}}, which renames folders on disk to match the kinds' names. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
match-title: Title of the dialog that renames the book's folders on disk so each matches its kind of page's current name.
match-hint: Explanation at the top of the {{msg-plotdevice|match-title}} dialog. "Links" are links in the book's text to the pages being moved. Full sentences.
match-links: Summary in the {{msg-plotdevice|match-title}} dialog of what renaming the folders will change. $1: how many links in the text will be updated; $2: how many files contain them.
match-no-links: Shown instead of {{msg-plotdevice|match-links}} in the {{msg-plotdevice|match-title}} dialog when no links need updating. A full sentence.
match-blocked-exists: Warning beside a folder in the {{msg-plotdevice|match-title}} dialog that can't be renamed because a folder with the new name already exists. A full sentence.
match-blocked-case-only: Warning beside a folder in the {{msg-plotdevice|match-title}} dialog when the old and new names differ only in upper- and lower-case letters, which the app can't rename safely; the author can do it in their computer's file manager. Full sentences.
match-blocked-invalid-name: Warning beside a folder in the {{msg-plotdevice|match-title}} dialog when the kind's name can't be a folder name (for example it has characters not allowed in file names). A full sentence.
match-blocked-other-files: Warning beside a folder in the {{msg-plotdevice|match-title}} dialog when the folder holds files other than pages, so it isn't renamed. A full sentence.
match-blocked-missing: Warning beside a folder in the {{msg-plotdevice|match-title}} dialog when the folder no longer exists on disk. A full sentence.
match-backup-title: Heading in the {{msg-plotdevice|match-title}} dialog, before the folders are renamed, recommending a backup copy of the book.
match-backup-hint: Explanation under {{msg-plotdevice|match-backup-title}} in the {{msg-plotdevice|match-title}} dialog. Full sentences.
match-backup-now: Button in the {{msg-plotdevice|match-title}} dialog that makes a backup copy of the whole book before renaming folders. Keep it short: it's a button.
match-backup-made: Confirmation after {{msg-plotdevice|match-backup-now}}, followed by the backup's folder path on the computer (shown after the colon, left to right).
match-backup-failed: Warning in the "Match folder names" dialog ({{msg-plotdevice|match-title}}), shown when the backup made with {{msg-plotdevice|match-backup-now}} could not be saved to the place the author chose. A full sentence.
match-have-backup: Checkbox label in the "Match folder names" dialog ({{msg-plotdevice|match-title}}). The author ticks it to say they already keep their own backup of the book, which allows {{msg-plotdevice|match-rename}} without making one now. Written in the author's voice ("I").
match-rename: Main button of the "Match folder names" dialog ({{msg-plotdevice|match-title}}). It renames the folders that hold the book's pages to match their kind of page's name, and updates every link to those pages. Keep it short: it's a button.
match-nothing: Warning in the "Match folder names" dialog ({{msg-plotdevice|match-title}}), shown instead of the backup step when none of the listed folders can be renamed (for example, a folder of that name already exists). A full sentence.
folders-renamed: Short notice at the bottom of the window after the "Match folder names" dialog renamed the folders. It comes with an {{msg-plotdevice|outline-undo}} button. $1: the number of links in chapters, outlines and pages that were updated to the new folder names.
folders-undo: Item in the book menu (opened from the book's name at the top), shown after folders were renamed with {{msg-plotdevice|match-rename}}, until the book is closed. It puts the old folder names and links back.
folders-undone: Short notice at the bottom of the window after {{msg-plotdevice|folders-undo}} put the old folder names and links back. A full sentence.
folders-undo-stale: Notice at the bottom of the window when {{msg-plotdevice|folders-undo}} is refused because files in the book changed after the rename (for example, in another app), so undoing would overwrite them. A full sentence.
folders-failed: Error notice at the bottom of the window when renaming the folders, or undoing the rename, failed. A full sentence.
story-new-kind: Link at the end of the World group in the Story workspace's sidebar, with "+" added in front by the code. It opens the "Kinds of pages" dialog ({{msg-plotdevice|kinds-menu}}) to add a kind of page of the book's own, such as Factions. Keep it short.
story-manuscript: Entry in the Plot group of the Story workspace's sidebar, and the heading of the screen it opens. That screen shows the book's parts and chapters in reading order, for reference while planning. "Chapters" here is the general word, even if the book renames chapters (e.g. "Sessions").
story-manuscript-hint: Explanation under the heading {{msg-plotdevice|story-manuscript}} in the Story workspace. "Write" is the name of the writing workspace ({{msg-plotdevice|workspace-write}}); use the same translation. Two full sentences.
prompt-outline-title: Label of the text box in the small dialog that asks for an outline's name: when creating a new outline, renaming one, or starting a character's arc from a page. Keep it short: it's a field label.
new-outline-start: Label of the choice in the new-outline dialog, below {{msg-plotdevice|prompt-outline-title}}. The author picks a ready-made shape for the outline: {{msg-plotdevice|starter-empty}}, {{msg-plotdevice|starter-three-acts}}, and so on. A fragment, like "Start from: Three acts".
starter-empty: Option under {{msg-plotdevice|new-outline-start}} in the new-outline dialog: start with an outline that has no sections or cards. Keep it short.
starter-three-acts: Option under {{msg-plotdevice|new-outline-start}} in the new-outline dialog: a ready-made outline with three sections, the classic three-act structure of a story (setup, confrontation, resolution). Use the usual term for this structure in your language.
starter-story-beats: Option under {{msg-plotdevice|new-outline-start}} in the new-outline dialog: a ready-made outline of the common turning points ("beats") of a novel's plot, such as the inciting incident and the climax. Use the term writers in your language use, if there is one.
starter-character-arc: Option under {{msg-plotdevice|new-outline-start}} in the new-outline dialog: a ready-made outline that follows how one character changes over the story. Use the usual writers' term for "character arc" in your language.
starter-campaign-arc: Option under {{msg-plotdevice|new-outline-start}} in the new-outline dialog: a ready-made outline for the overall storyline of a tabletop role-playing campaign (such as Dungeons & Dragons), across many game sessions.
starter-session-plan: Option under {{msg-plotdevice|new-outline-start}} in the new-outline dialog: a ready-made outline for planning one game session of a tabletop role-playing campaign (such as Dungeons & Dragons).
outline-guide: Short guide shown above an outline in the Story workspace, the first time the author opens one. It explains sections (big steps, shown as columns on the Board), cards (moments within a section) and details (sub-points under a card). Use the same words as in {{msg-plotdevice|outline-add-section}}, {{msg-plotdevice|outline-add-card}} and {{msg-plotdevice|outline-add-detail}}.
outline-guide-done: Button under the outline guide ({{msg-plotdevice|outline-guide}}). It closes the guide for good. Keep it short: it's a button.
view-switch: Screen-reader-only label (aria-label) for the group of buttons above an outline that switch how it is shown: {{msg-plotdevice|view-board}}, {{msg-plotdevice|view-outline}} or {{msg-plotdevice|view-text}}.
view-board: Button above an outline in the Story workspace, one of three that switch how the outline is shown. The Board shows each section as a column of cards. Keep it short: it's a button.
view-outline: Button above an outline in the Story workspace, one of three that switch how the outline is shown. It shows the whole outline as one indented list. Keep it short: it's a button.
view-text: Button above an outline in the Story workspace, one of three that switch how the outline is shown. It shows the outline as plain text that the author types freely. Keep it short: it's a button.
view-text-title: Tooltip of the {{msg-plotdevice|view-text}} button above an outline. $1: the keyboard shortcut, "Ctrl+Shift+E" or "⌘⇧E" on a Mac; don't translate it.
outline-text: Screen-reader-only label (aria-label) of the text editor in the Text view of an outline ({{msg-plotdevice|view-text}}).
outline-text-hint: Help line above the text editor in the Text view of an outline. A "card" is a moment in the outline, a "detail" a sub-point under a card, a "section" a big step; "@" starts a link to a page (a character, place or note). $1: the shortcut that goes back to the previous view, "Ctrl+Shift+E" or "⌘⇧E"; $2: the shortcut that makes a line a section, "Ctrl+Alt+2" or "⌘⌥2". Don't translate the key names Enter and Tab, or "@".
outline-text-kept: Note below the text editor in the Text view of an outline. $1: the number of passages written in a way the Board can't show; they appear on the Board in a box labelled {{msg-plotdevice|kept-as-written}}, so use the same words. Followed by the {{msg-plotdevice|outline-text-show-kept}} button.
outline-text-show-kept: Small link-style button after {{msg-plotdevice|outline-text-kept}} in the Text view of an outline. It jumps to the passages kept as written. Keep it short.
outline-undo: Item in the ⋯ menu beside an outline's views, which undoes the last change to the outline; also the button on short notices at the bottom of the window, e.g. after {{msg-plotdevice|folders-renamed}}. Keep it short: a menu item and a button.
outline-add-section: Button at the end of an outline, after the last column on the Board or the last section in the List, that adds a new section (a big step of the story). "+" is added in front by the code. Keep it short.
outline-add-card: Button at the bottom of a section's column on the Board, and an item in a section's menu, that adds a new card (a moment within the section). "+" is added in front by the code on the Board. Keep it short.
outline-add-detail: Item in a card's menu, and the tooltip and screen-reader label of the {{msg-plotdevice|outline-detail}} button in the List view, that adds a detail (a sub-point) under the card. Keep it short.
outline-add-item: Button under a section in the List view of an outline, that starts a new item at the section's end. An item is a line of the outline: a card, or a detail under one. "+" is added in front by the code. Keep it short.
prompt-item-text: Screen-reader label (aria-label) of the text box for editing an item in the List view of an outline. An item is a line of the outline: a card or a detail.
item-link-hint: Hint under the text box while the author edits a card, detail or item in an outline. "@" starts a link to a page or chapter; don't translate it. Other messages build on this one: it may follow {{msg-plotdevice|outline-line-keys}}, separated by " · ".
outline-line-keys: Hint under the text box while the author edits a line of an outline: the keys to press. Don't translate the key names (Enter, Tab, Shift+Tab, Esc); translate only what they do. The " · " separates the parts. {{msg-plotdevice|item-link-hint}} is added after it.
outline-add-item-to: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the small "+" button beside a section's name in the List view of an outline. $1: the section's name, e.g. "The Crossing".
outline-detail: Small button that appears when the author points at an item in the List view of an outline; it adds a detail under that item. "+ " is added in front by the code. Keep it very short: one word.
line-new-item: Placeholder in the empty text box for a new item in the List view of an outline. An item is a line of the outline, a card.
line-new-detail: Placeholder (and screen-reader label) in the empty text box for a new detail under a card or item in an outline. $1: the card's text, in quotation marks, e.g. "The ferry sinks".
line-keys-next-item: Part of the key hint under the text box for a new line in the List view of an outline; the parts are joined with " · ". Don't translate "Enter". Pressing it starts the next item.
line-keys-next-detail: Part of the key hint under the text box for a new detail in the List view of an outline; the parts are joined with " · ". Don't translate "Enter". Pressing it starts the next detail.
line-keys-nest: Part of the key hint under the text box for a new line in the List view of an outline; the parts are joined with " · ". Don't translate "Tab". $1: the text of the line above, in quotation marks, which the new line would become a detail of.
line-keys-out-item: Part of the key hint under the text box for a new detail in the List view of an outline; the parts are joined with " · ". Don't translate "Shift+Tab". Pressing it turns the detail into an item of its own (a card).
line-keys-out: Part of the key hint under the text box for a new detail nested two or more levels deep in the List view of an outline; the parts are joined with " · ". Don't translate "Shift+Tab". Pressing it moves the line one level out.
line-keys-done: Part of the key hint under the text box for a new line in the List view of an outline; the parts are joined with " · ". Don't translate "Esc". Pressing it stops adding lines.
line-keys-link: Last part of the key hint under the text box for a new line in the List view of an outline; the parts are joined with " · ". Typing "@" starts a link to a page; don't translate "@". Keep it very short.
outline-empty: Shown in place of an outline's contents when it has no sections or cards yet. Two short sentences.
outline-unnamed-section: Name shown for the first column on the Board (or group in the List) when an outline has cards before its first section heading. It stands where a section's name would be.
outline-rename-title: Item in the ⋯ menu beside an outline's views, and the tooltip of the outline's name at the top, that renames the outline. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
outline-actions: Screen-reader-only label (aria-label) of the ⋯ menu button beside an outline's views, which holds {{msg-plotdevice|outline-undo}}, {{msg-plotdevice|outline-rename-title}} and {{msg-plotdevice|outline-versions}}.
outline-versions: Item in the ⋯ menu beside an outline's views. It opens a window listing earlier saved versions of the outline, to look at or bring back. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
item-actions: Screen-reader-only label (aria-label) of the ⋯ menu button on a card or item in an outline. $1: the card's text, e.g. "The ferry sinks".
section-actions: Screen-reader-only label (aria-label) of the ⋯ menu button beside a section's name in an outline. $1: the section's name, e.g. "The Crossing".
item-edit: Item in a card's ⋯ menu in an outline. It opens the card's text for editing in place. The ellipsis means more input follows.
item-delete: Item in a card's ⋯ menu in an outline. It deletes the card, after asking ({{msg-plotdevice|confirm-delete-item}}). The ellipsis means a confirmation dialog follows.
item-collapse: Screen-reader-only label (aria-label) of the small arrow before an item with details in the List view of an outline. It hides the item's details. Replaced by {{msg-plotdevice|item-expand}} while they are hidden.
item-expand: Screen-reader-only label (aria-label) of the small arrow before an item whose details are hidden in the List view of an outline. It shows them again. Replaced by {{msg-plotdevice|item-collapse}} while they are shown.
item-move-earlier: Menu item that moves a card one place up within its section of an outline; also in the menu of a page on the shelf (the References panel beside the chapter), where it moves the page one place up. Keep it short.
item-move-later: Menu item that moves a card one place down within its section of an outline; also in the menu of a page on the shelf (the References panel beside the chapter), where it moves the page one place down. Keep it short.
move-to-section: Item in a card's ⋯ menu in an outline, one per other section. It moves the card to the end of that section. $1: the section's name, e.g. "The Crossing".
section-rename: Item in a section's ⋯ menu in an outline. It opens the section's name for editing in place. The ellipsis means more input follows.
section-move-earlier: Item in a section's ⋯ menu in an outline. It moves the whole section one place earlier (one column to the left on the Board in a left-to-right language).
section-move-later: Item in a section's ⋯ menu in an outline. It moves the whole section one place later (one column to the right on the Board in a left-to-right language).
section-delete: Item in a section's ⋯ menu in an outline. It deletes the section and all its cards, after asking ({{msg-plotdevice|confirm-delete-section}}). The ellipsis means a confirmation dialog follows.
prompt-section-name: Screen-reader label (aria-label) of the text box for a section's name, when adding or renaming a section in an outline.
prompt-card-text: Screen-reader label (aria-label) of the text box for a card's text, when adding or editing a card on the Board of an outline.
confirm-delete-item: Question in the confirmation dialog before deleting a card or item from an outline. $1: the card's text, e.g. "The ferry sinks". "Everything inside it" means its details. The button is {{msg-plotdevice|confirm-delete}}.
confirm-delete-section: Question in the confirmation dialog before deleting a section of an outline. $1: the section's name, e.g. "The Crossing". The button is {{msg-plotdevice|confirm-delete}}.
confirm-delete: Button in the confirmation dialog that deletes the card or section ({{msg-plotdevice|confirm-delete-item}}, {{msg-plotdevice|confirm-delete-section}}). Keep it short: it's a button.
details-count: Shown at the bottom of a card on the Board when it has more than three details. $1: the number of details (sub-points under the card).
kept-as-written: Label of a small fold-out box on the Board, in the List, on a page or in a chapter, around a passage the app can't show in its usual way; the passage is kept exactly as the author wrote it in the file. Clicking it shows {{msg-plotdevice|kept-explanation}}.
kept-explanation: Explanation inside (and tooltip of) the {{msg-plotdevice|kept-as-written}} box. "Text" is the outline's Text view, {{msg-plotdevice|view-text}}; use the same translation. Two full sentences.
locked-item: Tooltip and screen-reader label of a 🔒 icon on a card in an outline. The card's line in the file also holds other Markdown formatting, so it can't be moved. "Markdown" is the name of the text format; usually not translated.
invalid-details: Warning above an outline when the details at the top of its file (its name and settings, stored in the file's header) can't be read. "Details" here means the file's information, not the details under cards. Two full sentences.
outline-changed-elsewhere: Notice at the bottom of the window when a change to an outline was refused because the outline's file was changed by another app; the outline was reloaded so the author can try again.
outline-undo-refused: Notice at the bottom of the window when {{msg-plotdevice|outline-undo}} is refused because another app changed the outline after the author's last change. A full sentence.
outline-refused-unnamed-section: Notice at the bottom of the window when the author tries to change cards that sit above the outline's first section (shown under {{msg-plotdevice|outline-unnamed-section}}).
outline-refused-multiline-heading: Notice at the bottom of the window when a section's name can't be changed because, in the file, its heading is written over two lines. "Text editor" means any other app for plain text files.
outline-failed: Error notice at the bottom of the window when a change to an outline couldn't be made. Two short sentences.
story-character: Name of the Characters kind of page: an entry in the World group of the Story workspace's sidebar, and the heading of the gallery of character pages. Plural. The singular is {{msg-plotdevice|kind-character}}.
story-place: Name of the Places kind of page: an entry in the World group of the Story workspace's sidebar, and the heading of the gallery of place pages. Plural. The singular is {{msg-plotdevice|kind-place}}.
story-note: Name of the Notes kind of page: an entry in the World group of the Story workspace's sidebar, and the heading of the gallery of note pages (pages of any other information about the story's world). Plural. The singular is {{msg-plotdevice|kind-note}}.
new-character: The last card in the gallery of Characters in the Story workspace; it adds a new character page. "+" is added in front by the code. Keep it short.
new-place: The last card in the gallery of Places in the Story workspace; it adds a new place page. "+" is added in front by the code. Keep it short.
new-note: The last card in the gallery of Notes in the Story workspace; it adds a new note page. "+" is added in front by the code. Keep it short.
prompt-reference-title: Label of the text box in the small dialog that asks for a page's name, when adding or renaming a character, place, note or other page. Keep it short: it's a field label.
reference-rename: Item in a page's ⋯ menu in the Story workspace. It renames the page (its title, not its file). The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
reference-aka: Line under a page's name, on the page and on its card in the gallery, listing its other names. $1: the other names, joined with commas, e.g. "Old Mara, the Ferrywoman".
reference-hint: Help line above the text of a character, place or note page. "Description" is the short text shown on the page's card; "details" is the rest of the page. A full sentence.
reference-failed: Error notice at the bottom of the window when adding, renaming or changing a page (a character, place or note) failed. Two short sentences.
story-back-to: Screen-reader-only label (aria-label) of the link at the top of a page that goes back to its gallery. $1: the plural name of the kind of page, e.g. "Characters" or "Factions".
gallery-pages: Count of pages shown beside a kind of page or a tag, in the "Kinds of pages" dialog, the "Match folder names" dialog and the tidy-tags dialog. $1: the number of pages.
board-showing-about: Small label above the Board when it shows only the cards that link to one page (after {{msg-plotdevice|show-on-board}} on that page). $1: the page's name, e.g. "Mara". Followed by a ✕ button, {{msg-plotdevice|board-show-all}}.
board-show-all: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the ✕ button after {{msg-plotdevice|board-showing-about}} above the Board. It shows every card of the outline again.
page-actions: Screen-reader-only label (aria-label) of the ⋯ menu button at the top of a character, place or note page.
connections: Screen-reader-only label (aria-label) of the panel beside a page that lists its {{msg-plotdevice|relationships}} and what links to it.
relationships: Heading of the box beside a character, place or note page that lists how it is related to other pages, e.g. "Aunt of Ilka".
relationships-folded: One line shown inside a page's text, in place of the section of the file that holds its relationships, because they are already listed beside the page under {{msg-plotdevice|relationships}}.
relationship-add: Button under {{msg-plotdevice|relationships}} beside a page. It picks another page, then asks how they're related. "+" is added in front by the code. Keep it short.
relationship-actions: Screen-reader-only label (aria-label) of the ⋯ menu button on one relationship beside a page. $1: the relationship as written, e.g. "Sister of Ilka".
relationship-reword: Item in a relationship's ⋯ menu beside a page. It changes the words that say how the two pages are related, e.g. "Sister of". The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
relationship-remove: Item in a relationship's ⋯ menu beside a page, and the button of the confirmation dialog ({{msg-plotdevice|confirm-remove-relationship}}). It removes the relationship, not the other page. Keep it short.
confirm-remove-relationship: Question in the confirmation dialog before removing a relationship beside a page. $1: the relationship as written, e.g. "Sister of Ilka".
prompt-relationship-words: Question in the small dialog after the author picks a page with {{msg-plotdevice|relationship-add}}. $1: the current page's name, e.g. "Mara"; $2: the picked page's name, e.g. "Ilka". The example should be a short phrase that reads before the other page's name; translate it naturally for your language.
prompt-relationship-reword: Label of the text box in the dialog opened by {{msg-plotdevice|relationship-reword}}, holding the words that say how the two pages are related, e.g. "Sister of".
relationship-changed-elsewhere: Notice shown when a change to a page (a relationship or its tags) couldn't be saved because the page's file was changed by another program in the meantime. The page has been reloaded, so the author can make the change again.
tags: Screen-reader-only label (aria-label) for the group of tags on a page, and on page cards in the World gallery and on the References shelf. A tag is a short word the author attaches to pages to group them.
tag-add: Button after a page's tags that opens a field for adding a new tag. The "+ " is part of the text. Keep it short: it sits among the tags as a small pill. Screen readers hear {{msg-plotdevice|tag-add-label}} instead.
tag-add-label: Screen-reader-only label (aria-label) for the {{msg-plotdevice|tag-add}} button and the field it opens on a page.
tag-remove: Tooltip and screen-reader label for the small × on one of a page's tags. $1: the tag, e.g. "villain".
tag-create: Suggestion at the end of the list under the new-tag field on a page, when what the author typed isn't an existing tag; choosing it creates the tag. $1: the text the author typed, e.g. "smugglers".
tags-failed: Error notice when adding or removing a tag on a page failed. Two short sentences; the second reassures that the page was left as it was.
tags-unreadable: Error notice when a page's tags can't be changed because the details block at the top of its file (where tags are stored) is damaged or can't be read. The author can fix it by hand in the page's plain text.
tag-filter: Screen-reader-only label (aria-label) for the row of tags above the pages in the World gallery and on the References shelf; choosing tags groups the pages under them.
tag-more: Button at the end of a row of tags, when not all of them fit, that opens the rest; also shown on page cards when a page has more tags than are shown. $1: how many more tags there are, e.g. 4. The "+ " is part of the text. Keep it short.
tag-more-label: Screen-reader-only label (aria-label) for the panel opened by {{msg-plotdevice|tag-more}}, which lists the tags that didn't fit in the row.
tag-find: Placeholder and screen-reader label for the search field in the panel opened by {{msg-plotdevice|tag-more}}, for finding a tag by typing.
tag-all-pages: Group heading on the References shelf and in the link picker, when pages are grouped by the chosen tags: the remaining pages that don't have them. $1: how many pages are in this group, e.g. 12. Shown as a number in parentheses, so no plural is needed.
tag-all-character: Group heading in the Characters gallery (World in the Story workspace) when pages are grouped by the chosen tags: the remaining characters. $1: how many characters are in this group, e.g. 12. Shown as a number in parentheses.
tag-all-place: Group heading in the Places gallery (World in the Story workspace) when pages are grouped by the chosen tags: the remaining places. $1: how many places are in this group, e.g. 12. Shown as a number in parentheses.
tag-all-note: Group heading in the Notes gallery (World in the Story workspace) when pages are grouped by the chosen tags: the remaining notes. $1: how many notes are in this group, e.g. 12. Shown as a number in parentheses.
tag-actions: Screen-reader-only label for the menu of actions on a tag, opened by right-clicking (or Shift+F10 on) a tag in the row of tags in the World gallery or on the References shelf. $1: the tag, e.g. "villain".
tag-rename-everywhere: Item in a tag's actions menu (right-click on a tag in the World gallery or on the References shelf): renames the tag on every page that has it. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
tag-remove-everywhere: Item in a tag's actions menu (right-click on a tag in the World gallery or on the References shelf): removes the tag from every page that has it, without deleting the pages. The ellipsis means a confirmation follows.
prompt-tag-rename: Question in the dialog opened by {{msg-plotdevice|tag-rename-everywhere}}, above a field holding the tag's name. $1: the tag being renamed, e.g. "villain"; $2: how many pages have the tag. The second sentence explains that typing the name of another existing tag merges the two tags into one.
confirm-tag-remove: Confirmation question after {{msg-plotdevice|tag-remove-everywhere}}. $1: the tag, e.g. "villain"; $2: how many pages have the tag. The confirming button is {{msg-plotdevice|tag-remove-action}}.
tag-remove-action: Confirming button in the dialog that asks {{msg-plotdevice|confirm-tag-remove}}. Keep it short: it's a button.
tag-retagged: Notice after a tag was renamed or removed on every page. $1: how many pages were changed.
tag-retagged-skipped: Notice after a tag was renamed or removed everywhere, when some pages couldn't be changed. $1: how many pages were changed; $2: how many pages couldn't be changed; $3: the titles of those pages, separated by commas, e.g. "Ilka, The Salt Orchard".
tags-need-tidying: Notice shown when the app finds tags that may need attention, such as two spellings of what looks like the same tag, or pages whose tags can't be read. $1: how many problems were found, shown in parentheses. It comes with a {{msg-plotdevice|tidy-tags}} button.
tidy-tags: Button that opens the {{msg-plotdevice|tidy-tags-title}} dialog; shown beside the tags in the World gallery and on the References shelf, and with the {{msg-plotdevice|tags-need-tidying}} notice. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
tidy-tags-title: Title of the dialog for tidying tags: merging tags that look like duplicates, and finding pages whose tags can't be read.
tidy-duplicates: Heading in the {{msg-plotdevice|tidy-tags-title}} dialog, above pairs of tags that seem to be the same tag spelled differently, e.g. "villain" and "Villain".
tidy-merge-into: Button beside a pair of similar tags in the {{msg-plotdevice|tidy-tags-title}} dialog: it replaces the other tag with this one on every page. Each pair has two of these buttons, one for each spelling. $1: the tag to keep, e.g. "villain".
tidy-unreadable: Heading in the {{msg-plotdevice|tidy-tags-title}} dialog, above the list of pages whose details block at the top of the file is damaged, so their tags can't be read.
tidy-open-page: Button beside a page in the {{msg-plotdevice|tidy-tags-title}} dialog, under {{msg-plotdevice|tidy-unreadable}}; it opens the page so the author can fix it by hand. Keep it short.
tidy-done: Shown in the {{msg-plotdevice|tidy-tags-title}} dialog when there are no tag problems left.
tidy-close: Button that closes the {{msg-plotdevice|tidy-tags-title}} dialog. Keep it short: it's a button.
linked-from: Heading of a section at the bottom of a page (a character, place or note) listing the outlines, pages and chapters that link to it.
linked-from-none: Shown under {{msg-plotdevice|linked-from}} on a page when nothing links to it yet. “Link to…” refers to the card menu item {{msg-plotdevice|link-to}} and should match its translation.
linked-from-pages: Subheading under {{msg-plotdevice|linked-from}} on a page, above the other pages (characters, places, notes) that link to it.
linked-from-chapters: Subheading under {{msg-plotdevice|linked-from}} on a page, above the chapters that link to it.
show-on-board: Button beside an outline listed under {{msg-plotdevice|linked-from}} on a page: opens that outline as a Board (columns of cards), with this page's cards highlighted and the others dimmed.
arc-start: Button at the bottom of a page (a character, place or note), shown with "+" added in front by the code: creates a new outline for this character's (or place's, or idea's) own story, linked to the page. An "arc" is the path of a character's story. {{msg-plotdevice|arc-start-hint}} is shown under it.
arc-start-hint: Small explanation under the {{msg-plotdevice|arc-start}} button on a page. $1: the page's title, e.g. "Ilka". A fragment, without a final period.
arc-outline-title: Suggested title for a new outline made with {{msg-plotdevice|arc-start}}, filled into the title field; the author can change it. $1: the page's title, e.g. "Ilka".
shelf: Name of the References panel beside the chapter in the Write workspace, which shows character, place and note pages while writing. Used as the tooltip and screen-reader label of the button that opens it, and in the guide. Other messages refer to it by this name.
shelf-search: Placeholder and screen-reader label for the search field at the top of the References panel ({{msg-plotdevice|shelf}}) in the Write workspace.
shelf-no-results: Shown on the References panel ({{msg-plotdevice|shelf}}) and in the link picker when a search finds nothing.
shelf-empty: Shown on the References panel ({{msg-plotdevice|shelf}}) in the Write workspace when no pages are open or pinned on it yet. "Pin" refers to {{msg-plotdevice|shelf-pin}}.
shelf-from-outline: Heading on the References panel ({{msg-plotdevice|shelf}}) in the Write workspace, above the outline cards that link to the chapter being written, with the characters and places they mention.
shelf-pin: Tooltip and screen-reader label for the pin button on a page's card on the References panel; pinning keeps the page there while the author moves between chapters. Becomes {{msg-plotdevice|shelf-unpin}} once pinned.
shelf-unpin: Replaces {{msg-plotdevice|shelf-pin}} on a page's card on the References panel once the page is pinned.
shelf-close: Item in the ⋯ menu of a page's card on the References panel: removes the card from the panel (the page itself stays). Keep it short.
shelf-edit: Item in the ⋯ menu of a page's card on the References panel: opens the page itself for editing in the Story workspace.
shelf-details: Label for the first part of a page's card on the References panel: the page's details (such as age or role) that come before its first heading. Shown like a heading, beside the page's own headings.
shelf-aka: Line under a page's name on its References panel card, listing the other names the character or place is known by. $1: the other names, separated by commas, e.g. "Bea, Aunt B". A fragment: "also" means "also known as".
shelf-show-details: Tooltip and screen-reader label for the button on a page's card on the References panel that opens all its parts at once. Becomes {{msg-plotdevice|shelf-hide-details}} when they're open.
shelf-hide-details: Replaces {{msg-plotdevice|shelf-show-details}} on a page's card on the References panel when all its parts are open; folds them again.
