resize-navigator: Screen-reader-only label for the handle that is dragged to change the width of the sidebar on the left (the list of chapters in Write, the Plot/World sidebar in Story).
resize-shelf: Screen-reader-only label for the handle that is dragged to change the width of the References panel in the Write workspace. "References" should match {{msg-plotdevice|shelf}}.
shelf-card-actions: Screen-reader-only label (aria-label) for the ⋯ menu button on a page's card on the References panel. $1: the page's title, e.g. "Ilka".
link-to: Item in an outline card's ⋯ menu, and tooltip of a button in the card's text field: links the card to a chapter, character, place or note, chosen from a list. The ellipsis means a picker follows.
link-search: Heading and screen-reader label of the picker opened by {{msg-plotdevice|link-to}}, with a field to type in to find what to link the card to. Works as an instruction or a placeholder.
unit-poem: What a poetry collection calls one chapter (the Poetry collection template). Also used to recognise the word in a book written in any language, so it must be the same word the template writes.
unit-poem-many: Plural of unit-poem: the sidebar's name for a poetry collection's chapters.
unit-poem-number: A poem's number in a poetry collection, beside the chapter menu and in the timeline. $1 is the number.
unit-poem-new: Sidebar button that adds a poem to a poetry collection, after a +.
unit-poem-none: Title of the empty Write view in a poetry collection with no poems.
unit-session: What a D&D campaign calls one chapter (the campaign template). Also used to recognise the word in a book written in any language, so it must be the same word the template writes.
unit-session-many: Plural of unit-session: the sidebar's name for a campaign's sessions.
unit-session-number: A session's number in a campaign, beside the chapter menu and in the timeline. $1 is the number.
unit-session-new: Sidebar button that adds a session to a campaign, after a +.
unit-session-none: Title of the empty Write view in a campaign with no sessions.
unit-section: What a poetry collection calls a part, a group of poems (ADR 0013). Also used to recognise the word in a book written in any language, so it must be the same word the template writes.
unit-section-new: Sidebar button that adds a section (a group of poems) to a poetry collection, after a +.
unit-section-rename: Item in a section's ⋯ menu. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
unit-section-name: Label in the small dialog that asks for a section's name.
kind-npc: A kind of page in the D&D campaign template: a non-player character. Also used to recognise the word in a book written in any language, so it must be the same word the template writes.
kind-location: A kind of page in the D&D campaign template: a place. Also used to recognise the word in a book written in any language, so it must be the same word the template writes.
kind-faction: A kind of page in the D&D campaign template: a group or organisation. Also used to recognise the word in a book written in any language, so it must be the same word the template writes.
kind-item: A kind of page in the D&D campaign template: an object. Also used to recognise the word in a book written in any language, so it must be the same word the template writes.
kind-lore: A kind of page in the D&D campaign template: background knowledge of the world. Also used to recognise the word in a book written in any language, so it must be the same word the template writes.
kind-chapter: One word saying what an item is, shown in search results and links: a chapter. Replaced by the book's own word for a chapter when the book renames it (e.g. "Session"). Singular, capitalised like a label.
kind-character: One word saying what an item is, shown on References panel cards, in search results and links: a character page. Singular, capitalised like a label.
kind-place: One word saying what an item is, shown on References panel cards, in search results and links: a place page. Singular, capitalised like a label.
kind-note: One word saying what an item is, shown on References panel cards, in search results and links: a note page (any other page of background material). Singular, capitalised like a label.
kind-outline: One word saying what an item is, shown in search results and links: an outline (a plan of sections and cards). Singular, capitalised like a label.
kind-other: One word saying what an item is, shown in search results and links, for a file the app doesn't recognise as a chapter, page or outline. Singular, capitalised like a label.
version-copy-label: Added to the name of a copy made from an earlier version with {{msg-plotdevice|versions-copy}}; it becomes part of the new file's name, after the original title. $1: the date and time of that version, e.g. "3 Nov 2026, 14.05". Lower case, as it follows the title.
versions: Item in a page's ⋯ menu (a character, place or note) that opens the dialog of the page's earlier versions. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
chapter-versions: Item in the book menu (the book's title in the top bar) that opens the dialog of the current chapter's earlier versions. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
versions-title: Title of the dialog listing earlier versions of a chapter or page. $1: the chapter's or page's title, e.g. "The Crossing".
versions-none: Shown in the earlier-versions dialog when the chapter or page has no earlier versions yet. Explains that versions are saved automatically while the author writes, no more than once every ten minutes.
versions-restore: Button in the earlier-versions dialog that brings back the chosen version in place of the current text.
versions-restore-detail: Small reassurance in the earlier-versions dialog, near {{msg-plotdevice|versions-restore}}: restoring is safe because the current text is saved as a version first. Also used in the guide right after that button's name.
versions-copy: Button in the earlier-versions dialog that saves the chosen version as a separate new file, leaving the current text unchanged.
versions-copied: Notice after {{msg-plotdevice|versions-copy}} worked. $1: the new file's name, which includes {{msg-plotdevice|version-copy-label}}.
versions-stale: Error notice when restoring an earlier version was refused because the file was changed by another program after the versions dialog opened.
versions-failed: Error notice when restoring or copying an earlier version failed.
versions-close: Button that closes the earlier-versions dialog without doing anything. Keep it short: it's a button.
export-book: Item in the book menu (the book's title in the top bar): opens the Export window, to save the book as a Word file, a PDF, an e-book or Markdown. The ellipsis means a window follows.
import-add-menu: Item in the book menu (Milestone 23): adds chapters from a Word file (.docx) at the end of the open book, after a preview. The ellipsis means a file picker follows.
import-new-menu: Link under the templates in the New project form: makes the new book from a Word file (.docx) instead of a template. The ellipsis means a file picker follows.
import-new-hint: Shown beside {{msg-plotdevice|import-new-menu}}: what it's for. ".docx" is the Word file's extension.
import-new-from: In the New project form, after choosing a Word file: heading of the card that replaces the templates. $1: the file's name, e.g. "The Salt Orchard.docx".
import-new-chapters: In the New project form, under {{msg-plotdevice|import-new-from}}: how many chapters the new book will have. $1: the number. Supports PLURAL.
import-new-other-file: Link in the New project form: choose a different Word file. The ellipsis means a file picker follows.
import-new-use-template: Link in the New project form: forget the Word file and choose a template again.
import-new-create: The New project form's main button when the book is made from a Word file. $1: how many chapters. Supports PLURAL.
import-title: Heading of the import preview window. $1: the Word file's name, e.g. "The Salt Orchard.docx".
import-split-by: Label of the three ways of splitting a Word file into chapters, in the import preview.
import-split-headings: Choice in the import preview: split at Word's heading styles (Heading 1, Heading 2…).
import-split-chapter-lines: Choice in the import preview: split at lines that say "Chapter 3", "Chapter Three" and the like. Use your language's word for chapter in the quotes.
import-split-page-breaks: Choice in the import preview: split at each page break in the Word file.
import-split-headings-hint: One line under the split choice when {{msg-plotdevice|import-split-headings}} is chosen.
import-split-chapter-lines-hint: One line under the split choice when {{msg-plotdevice|import-split-chapter-lines}} is chosen. Give your language's own examples.
import-split-page-breaks-hint: One line under the split choice when {{msg-plotdevice|import-split-page-breaks}} is chosen.
import-found: Beside the split choice: how many chapters will come in. $1: the number. Supports PLURAL.
import-found-parts: Beside the split choice: how many chapters and parts will come in. $1: chapters; $2: parts. Supports PLURAL.
import-chapters: Accessible name of the list of chapters in the import preview.
import-keep: Accessible name of a chapter's checkbox in the import preview: whether to bring it in. $1: the chapter's name.
import-rename: Accessible name of a chapter's name field in the import preview. $1: its position in the list.
import-words: A chapter's word count in the import preview. $1: the number. Supports PLURAL.
import-list-hint: Under the list of chapters in the import preview: how to rename or leave out a chapter.
import-join: Link above a chapter's text in the import preview: makes it part of the chapter before it.
import-start-here: Small link that shows over a paragraph (on hover or keyboard focus) in the import preview: starts a new chapter at that paragraph.
import-left-out: In the import preview's note, before what won't come in (comments, pictures, tables).
import-left-comments: Part of the import preview's note: comments in the Word file, which won't come in. $1: how many. Supports PLURAL.
import-left-pictures: Part of the import preview's note: pictures in the Word file, which won't come in. $1: how many. Supports PLURAL.
import-left-tables: Part of the import preview's note: tables in the Word file, which won't come in. $1: how many. Supports PLURAL.
import-tracked-changes: In the import preview's note: tracked changes (Word's Track Changes) are taken as accepted, and the title page before the first chapter isn't brought in.
import-footnotes: In the import preview's note: footnotes are kept, listed at the end of their chapter. $1: how many. Supports PLURAL.
import-part-name: Label of a field in the import preview, when adding chapters to the open book: the name of the new part they go into at the end of the book.
import-next: The import preview's main button when making a new book: on to the book's details.
import-add: The import preview's main button when adding to the open book. $1: how many chapters. Supports PLURAL.
imported-chapters: Notice after chapters from a Word file were added. $1: how many. Supports PLURAL.
imported-chapters-details: Notice after chapters were added, when the Word file names a different title or author than the book; a {{msg-plotdevice|imported-use-details}} button follows. $1: how many chapters; $2: the file's title; $3: its author.
imported-use-details: Button on {{msg-plotdevice|imported-chapters-details}}: uses the Word file's title and author for the book.
import-failed-too-big: Notice when the chosen Word file is over 50 MB.
import-failed-not-a-word-file: Notice when the chosen file isn't a .docx Word file.
import-failed-old-or-protected: Notice when the chosen file is an old .doc file or a password-protected one.
import-failed-unreadable: Notice when the Word file is damaged or can't be read.
import-failed-no-project: Notice when adding chapters with no book open (rare).
import-failed-no-import: Notice when the Word file being imported was forgotten (rare).
import-failed-no-chapters: Notice when no chapter is ticked.
import-failed-stale: Notice when the book's contents changed (in another app) while the author was in the preview.
import-failed-invalid: Notice when the chapters couldn't be added to CONTENTS.md.
import-failed-write-failed: Notice when the new chapter files couldn't be saved.
import-failed-unreadable-book: Notice when the book's own contents file can't be read.
dialog-import-word: Title of the file picker for a Word file to bring in.
dialog-import-word-files: File type shown in that picker: Word documents (.docx).
export-title: Heading of the Export window, opened from {{msg-plotdevice|export-book}}.
export-format: Label above the four kinds of file in the Export window (Word, PDF, e-book, Markdown).
export-format-word: Choice in the Export window: a Word document (.docx). "Word" is Microsoft Word's name; keep it unless your language calls these files something else.
export-format-pdf: Choice in the Export window: a PDF file. Usually kept as "PDF".
export-format-epub: Choice in the Export window: an e-book file (EPUB), for e-book readers such as Kindle, Kobo or Apple Books.
export-format-markdown: Choice in the Export window: one Markdown file of the whole book. "Markdown" is a name; usually kept as it is.
export-format-word-hint: One line under the format choice in the Export window when Word is chosen: who the file is for. Word, Google Docs, LibreOffice and Pages are product names.
export-format-pdf-hint: One line under the format choice in the Export window when PDF is chosen: who the file is for.
export-format-epub-hint: One line under the format choice in the Export window when E-book is chosen. EPUB is the name of the file format.
export-format-markdown-hint: One line under the format choice in the Export window when Markdown is chosen.
export-title-page: Checkbox in the Export window (Word and PDF): whether the file starts with a title page showing the title, the author and the word count. On by default.
export-book-title: Label of the book's title field in the Export window. What the author types here is saved as the book's title.
export-book-author: Label of the author's name field in the Export window. What the author types here is saved with the book.
export-no-title: Warning under the title field in the Export window when the book has no title yet (or still has the placeholder "Untitled project").
export-author-hint-page: Hint under the author field in the Export window, for Word and PDF: where the name appears in the file.
export-author-hint-epub: Hint under the author field in the Export window, for an e-book: where the name appears.
export-author-hint-markdown: Hint under the author field in the Export window, for Markdown: where the name appears.
export-saves-details: Note in the Export window once the author has typed a different title or author: these are saved to the book itself when they export.
export-word-count: Checkbox in the Export window (Word and PDF, with a title page): whether the title page shows the book's word count. Followed by {{msg-plotdevice|export-word-count-about}} in brackets.
export-word-count-about: The rounded word count beside {{msg-plotdevice|export-word-count}}, in brackets. $1: the number, already formatted, e.g. "84,000".
export-chapters: Label of the chapter choice in the Export window: the whole book, or chosen chapters.
export-whole-book: Choice in the Export window: export every chapter. $1: how many chapters the book has. Supports PLURAL.
export-choose-chapters: Choice in the Export window: export only some chapters, ticked in a list that opens below. The ellipsis means more choices follow.
export-first-three: Small link above the chapter list in the Export window: ticks only the book's first three chapters, as agents and publishers often ask for a sample.
export-all: Small link above the chapter list in the Export window: ticks every chapter.
export-none: Small link above the chapter list in the Export window: unticks every chapter.
export-none-chosen: Shown under the chapter list in the Export window when no chapter is ticked; the Export button is disabled.
export-headings: Label of the chapter-heading choice in the Export window.
export-headings-both: Choice in the Export window: each chapter is headed by its number ("Chapter 1") and its name. Use your language's word for chapter, as in {{msg-plotdevice|export-file-chapter}}.
export-headings-name: Choice in the Export window: each chapter is headed by its name only, without "Chapter 1".
export-look: Label above the layout choices in the Export window (Word and PDF).
export-double: Checkbox in the Export window (Word and PDF): double line spacing, the standard for manuscripts sent to editors; 1.5 lines when off.
export-paper: Label of the paper size list in the Export window (Word and PDF). It starts from the computer's region.
export-paper-a4: Paper size: A4 (used in most of the world). Usually kept as "A4".
export-paper-letter: Paper size: US Letter (used in the United States and Canada).
export-cover: Label of the cover picture choice in the Export window (e-book only).
export-cover-choose: Button in the Export window (e-book): picks a picture for the e-book's cover. The ellipsis means a file picker follows.
export-cover-remove: Link in the Export window: removes the chosen cover picture from the e-book. The picture file itself isn't changed.
export-cover-optional: Shown beside {{msg-plotdevice|export-cover-choose}} when no cover is chosen: a cover is optional.
export-cover-missing: Warning in the Export window when the cover picture chosen last time is no longer where it was. $1: the picture's file name.
export-unreadable: Warning in the Export window when chapters listed in the book's contents can't be read. $1: their titles, separated by commas.
export-saves-as: Line above the buttons in the Export window: the suggested file name. $1: the name, e.g. "The Salt Orchard.docx".
export-go: The main button of the Export window. The ellipsis means a save dialog follows, to choose where the file goes.
exported: Notice after exporting, with a {{msg-plotdevice|export-show}} button. $1: the path of the saved file.
exported-missing: Notice after exporting when some chapters couldn't be read and were left out. $1: the path of the saved file; $2: the missing chapters' titles, separated by commas.
export-show: Button on the notice after exporting: shows the saved file in the computer's file manager (Finder, Explorer, Files).
export-failed-no-project: Notice when exporting while no book is open (rare).
export-failed-no-chapters: Notice when exporting with no chapter chosen.
export-failed-cover-unreadable: Notice when the e-book's cover picture can't be read, so nothing was exported.
export-failed-details-failed: Notice when the title or author typed in the Export window couldn't be saved to the book, so nothing was exported.
export-failed-write-failed: Notice when the exported file couldn't be saved where the author chose.
export-failed-export-failed: Notice when making the exported file failed for another reason.
export-file-chapter: Written INTO the exported file (not shown in the app), in the book's language: a chapter's number above its name. $1: the number. Also used in the e-book's table of contents.
export-file-word-count: Written INTO the exported file's title page, in the book's language: the rounded word count. $1: the number, formatted, e.g. "84,000".
export-file-by: Written INTO the exported file's title page, in the book's language, before the author's name: "by Ines Varga".
export-file-contents: Written INTO the e-book, in the book's language: the heading of its table of contents.
dialog-export-word: File type shown in the save dialog when exporting a Word document.
dialog-export-pdf: File type shown in the save dialog when exporting a PDF.
dialog-export-epub: File type shown in the save dialog when exporting an e-book.
dialog-export-markdown: File type shown in the save dialog when exporting Markdown.
dialog-export-cover: Title of the file picker for an e-book's cover picture.
dialog-export-cover-pictures: File type shown in the cover picture picker: picture files (JPEG, PNG, GIF, WebP).
reference-rename-file: Item in a page's ⋯ menu (a character, place or note): changes the name of the page's file on disk, not the page's title. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
prompt-file-name-page: Label of the field in the dialog opened by {{msg-plotdevice|reference-rename-file}}, holding the page's current file name.
about-made-by: Text before the author's name, "Moriel Schottlender" (a link), in the About Plot Device dialog. A fragment: the name follows it.
help-documentation: Item in the ☰ app menu, and a link in the About Plot Device dialog, that opens the app's guide website in the browser.
about: Item in the ☰ app menu that opens the About dialog (version, licence, credits). "Plot Device" is the product name: usually not translated.
about-license: Paragraph in the About Plot Device dialog stating the app's licence. "Plot Device" is the product name: usually not translated. "Free software" means freedom (open source), not price; keep the official name of the GNU General Public License as it is commonly given in your language.
about-yours: Paragraph in the About Plot Device dialog reassuring the author that the app's licence covers only the program, and their own writing stays theirs. "Plot Device" is the product name: usually not translated.
about-credits: Folding heading in the About Plot Device dialog that opens the list of third-party open-source components the app uses. $1: how many components, shown in parentheses.
about-full-license: Folding heading in the About Plot Device dialog that opens the full text of the GNU General Public License. The licence text is only in English, which the parentheses say.
update-available: Small button in the top bar, shown when a newer version of the app has been released; it opens a panel with {{msg-plotdevice|update-is-out}}, {{msg-plotdevice|update-download}} and {{msg-plotdevice|update-not-now}}. Keep it short.
update-is-out: Says a newer version has been released, in the update panel from the top bar and in the About Plot Device dialog. $1: the new version number, e.g. "1.4.0". "Plot Device" is the product name: usually not translated.
update-whats-new: Link in the About Plot Device dialog, after {{msg-plotdevice|update-is-out}}, that opens the new version's release notes in the browser.
update-download: Link that opens the download page for the new version in the browser; shown in the update panel and the About Plot Device dialog. Nothing is downloaded or installed by the app itself.
update-not-now: Button in the update panel from the top bar that hides the update notice for now. Keep it short: it's a button.
update-check: Button in the About Plot Device dialog that checks right away whether a newer version is out. Replaced by {{msg-plotdevice|update-checking}} while checking.
update-checking: Shown in the About Plot Device dialog while {{msg-plotdevice|update-check}} is in progress.
update-newest: Shown in the About Plot Device dialog after {{msg-plotdevice|update-check}} when the app is already up to date.
update-failed: Error shown in the About Plot Device dialog when {{msg-plotdevice|update-check}} couldn't reach the server.
settings-check-updates: Checkbox in the Settings dialog: when on, the app checks once a day for a newer version. Explained by {{msg-plotdevice|settings-check-updates-hint}}.
settings-check-updates-hint: Small explanation under the {{msg-plotdevice|settings-check-updates}} checkbox in the Settings dialog. "Plot Device" (the product name) and "GitHub" (the website where the app is published) are usually not translated.
settings-advanced: Heading of the last group of options in the Settings dialog, for options most authors won't need.
settings-plain-text: Checkbox in the Settings dialog, under {{msg-plotdevice|settings-advanced}}: when on, chapters, pages and outlines open in the plain-text view showing every Markdown mark (such as # and *), instead of formatted text. Written from the author's point of view ("I").
settings-plain-text-hint: Small explanation under the {{msg-plotdevice|settings-plain-text}} checkbox in the Settings dialog. "Mark" means a Markdown formatting symbol in the text, such as # for a heading or * for italics.
settings-plain-text-switch: Checkbox in the Settings dialog, under {{msg-plotdevice|settings-advanced}}: when on, a {{msg-plotdevice|plain-text-switch}} toggle shows beside the Format button on every chapter, page and outline text. Off by default, for authors who don't know Markdown.
settings-plain-text-switch-hint: Small explanation under the {{msg-plotdevice|settings-plain-text-switch}} checkbox. $1 is the keyboard shortcut, such as Ctrl+Shift+M. "Mark" means a Markdown formatting symbol, such as # or *.
report-problem: Item in the ☰ app menu that opens a short form on GitHub in the browser for reporting a bug. The ellipsis means a form follows.
suggest-idea: Item in the ☰ app menu that opens a short form on GitHub in the browser for suggesting a new feature. The ellipsis means a form follows.
about-coffee: Playful paragraph in the About Plot Device dialog asking for support. "Plot twist" and "the next chapter… of the code" are writing puns; a similar joke in your language is welcome. $1: a link whose text is {{msg-plotdevice|about-coffee-link}} (to the author's Buy Me a Coffee page); the sentence must read naturally with it in place. "Plot Device" is the product name: usually not translated.
about-coffee-link: Link text placed into {{msg-plotdevice|about-coffee}} in place of $1; it opens the author's Buy Me a Coffee page. "One" means a coffee. Must fit grammatically into that sentence.
story-timeline: Entry at the top of the Plot group in the Story workspace's sidebar, and the heading of the screen it opens: the book's outlines side by side, one row each, lined up in time (ADR 0012).
outline-main-badge: Small label beside the main outline's name in the sidebar's Plot group. The main outline's sections are the timeline's column names. One short word.
timeline-main-outline: Small label beside the top row's name on the timeline, saying that this outline is the main outline, whose sections name the columns. Lowercase in English: it follows the outline's name.
timeline-columns-from: Quiet line above the timeline, always shown, followed by the main outline's name in bold and then {{msg-plotdevice|timeline-change-main}}. Explains where the timeline's column names come from.
timeline-change-main: Link after {{msg-plotdevice|timeline-columns-from}} above the timeline. Opens a list of the book's other outlines, to make one of them the main outline.
timeline-columns-hint: Second half of the quiet line above the timeline. Says how to rename a column (click its name) and add one (the + between two columns). Each column is a section of the main outline.
timeline-rename-column: Tooltip of a column name on the timeline. $1: the main outline's name, e.g. "Main story".
timeline-add-section-here: Tooltip and screen-reader label of the + button between two columns of the timeline. $1: the main outline's name.
outline-make-main: Menu command for an outline (in its ⋯ menu, and on its timeline row). Its sections then name the timeline's columns. Nothing in the outlines changes.
main-swap-question: Question in a small dialog before another outline becomes the main outline. $1: that outline's name. Reassures the author that no file content changes.
timeline-hide: Menu command on a timeline row: hides that outline's row from the timeline only. The outline itself is not changed.
timeline-hidden: Quiet note under the timeline when the author has hidden rows. $1: how many. Followed by {{msg-plotdevice|timeline-show-all}}.
timeline-show-all: Button after {{msg-plotdevice|timeline-hidden}} that shows every hidden row of the timeline again.
timeline-storyline-actions: Screen-reader-only label of the ⋯ menu button on a timeline row. $1: the outline's name. A storyline is one outline shown as a row of the timeline.
timeline-storyline: Screen-reader-only label of a timeline row (a region). $1: the outline's name.
timeline-moment-actions: Screen-reader-only label of the ⋯ menu button on a section in a timeline row. $1: the section's name.
timeline-line-up: Menu command on a section in a timeline row. Opens a list of other outlines' sections; choosing one says this section happens at the same time.
timeline-line-up-again: Menu command on a section whose line-up can't be used any more; like {{msg-plotdevice|timeline-line-up}}.
timeline-unpin: Menu command on a lined-up section in a timeline row: it no longer happens at the same time as the other section. Removes one line from the outline.
timeline-line-up-title: Heading of the list of sections to line a section up with. $1: the section being lined up.
timeline-same-time-as: IMPORTANT: written into the author's outline file, in the book's language, before a link to another section, e.g. "At the same time as [The night of the storm]". Keep the trailing space in languages that need one.
timeline-lined-up-with: Tooltip of the ⇄ mark on a lined-up section (timeline, board and list). $1: the section it is lined up with.
timeline-not-lined-up: Screen-reader text after a section's name on the timeline when it isn't lined up with another outline: it just sits between its neighbours.
timeline-cant-line-up-missing: Tooltip and screen-reader text of a section whose line-up points to a section that was deleted or renamed outside the app. $1: the link's text.
timeline-cant-line-up-order: Tooltip and screen-reader text of a section whose line-up contradicts its outline's own order. $1: the section it points to.
timeline-add-card: Button in a timeline cell that adds a card to that section of that outline.
timeline-one-title: Heading shown on the timeline when the book has only one outline.
timeline-one-text: Text under {{msg-plotdevice|timeline-one-title}}, explaining what another storyline is for.
timeline-new-storyline: Button on the timeline that creates a new outline (it opens the same dialog as {{msg-plotdevice|story-new-outline}}) and shows it as a new row.
story-open-outline: Menu command on a timeline row: opens that outline on its own (Board, List or Text).
timeline-drag-section: Tooltip of a section's name in a timeline row. Dragging it onto a moment of another outline says the two happen at the same time. The same is in the section's ⋯ menu.
timeline-move-to: Menu command on a card in a timeline row: moves the card to another section of the same outline (the keyboard's way to drag it). $1: that section's name.
timeline-card-actions: Screen-reader-only label of the ⋯ menu button on a card in a timeline row. $1: the card's text.
outline-set-aside: Menu command for an outline (its ⋯ menu, and its timeline row): moves it to the quiet Set aside list at the end of Plot and off the timeline. Nothing is deleted; {{msg-plotdevice|outline-bring-back}} returns it.
outline-bring-back: Menu command for an outline that was set aside: returns it to the outlines in use and to the timeline.
story-set-aside: Small heading at the end of the Plot group in the sidebar, above outlines the author set aside. Shown only when there are some.
outline-delete: Menu command for an outline. Opens a confirmation ({{msg-plotdevice|outline-delete-question}}) before anything is deleted.
outline-delete-question: First line (the question) of the confirmation before an outline is deleted. $1: the outline's name. Followed by {{msg-plotdevice|outline-delete-what}}, {{msg-plotdevice|outline-delete-backup}}, and {{msg-plotdevice|outline-delete-suggest}}, each as its own short paragraph.
outline-delete-lined-up: Added to the delete confirmation when other outlines' sections are lined up (on the timeline) with the outline being deleted. $1: how many.
outline-delete-new-main: Added to the delete or set-aside confirmation when the main outline goes: $1 is the outline whose sections will name the timeline's columns instead.
outline-delete-action: Button that confirms deleting an outline: it goes to the computer's Trash (Recycle Bin).
outline-delete-for-good-question: Second, stronger confirmation shown only when moving to the Trash failed. $1: the outline's name.
outline-delete-for-good: Button that confirms {{msg-plotdevice|outline-delete-for-good-question}}: the outline is deleted and can't be got back.
outline-deleted: Notice after an outline was moved to the computer's Trash. $1: its name.
outline-deleted-for-good: Notice after an outline was deleted for good (there was no Trash). $1: its name.
outline-now-main: Notice after the main outline was set aside or deleted: $1 is the outline whose sections now name the timeline's columns.
outline-delete-failed: Notice when deleting an outline failed, e.g. the file changed in another program meanwhile.
outline-set-aside-instead: Button in the delete confirmation, shown as the recommended choice: sets the outline aside rather than deleting it (nothing is deleted).
outline-undo-delete: Button beside {{msg-plotdevice|outline-deleted}}: puts the deleted outline back exactly as it was.
outline-restored: Notice after undoing an outline's deletion. $1: its name.
outline-delete-what: Paragraph in the delete confirmation: what goes and what stays.
outline-delete-backup: Paragraph in the delete confirmation: where the outline goes (the computer's Trash or Recycle Bin), and that a backup is kept and the deletion can be undone.
outline-delete-suggest: Last paragraph of the delete confirmation, recommending {{msg-plotdevice|outline-set-aside-instead}}.
timeline-cant-line-up-fix: Follows {{msg-plotdevice|timeline-cant-line-up-missing}} or {{msg-plotdevice|timeline-cant-line-up-order}} under a section on the timeline: how to fix it, from the section's ⋯ menu.
timeline-no-choices: Shown, greyed out, in a section's line-up menu on the timeline when no moment of another outline keeps the storylines' order (e.g. the section comes before everything the others have).
backups-menu: Book menu item that opens the {{msg-plotdevice|backups-title}} window for the open book. The ellipsis means a window follows.
backups-title: Heading of the window, opened from the book menu, where the author chooses where this book's backups are kept, sees the last one, and can turn on a clean-up.
backups-what: Explanation at the top of the {{msg-plotdevice|backups-title}} window. "Plot Device" is the product name: usually not translated. "zip" is a file type: keep it as is, or use the word readers in your language know.
backups-where: Small heading in the {{msg-plotdevice|backups-title}} window, above the backup folder and the buttons for choosing one. "Them" means this book's backups.
backups-none: Shown in the {{msg-plotdevice|backups-title}} window while the book has no backup folder.
backups-sync-hint: Advice under the folder choice, in the {{msg-plotdevice|backups-title}} window and in the backup offer. The service names are product names: usually not translated. The point: backups are only local; a folder that a sync app keeps online gets them off the computer.
backups-use-folder: Button offering the folder chosen for another book's backups. $1: that folder's full path, e.g. "/home/ines/Dropbox/Backups".
backups-choose: Button that opens the system's folder picker, to choose where this book's backups go. The ellipsis means a dialog follows.
backups-choose-other: Same as {{msg-plotdevice|backups-choose}}, shown when the book already has a backup folder.
backups-open-folder: Button in the {{msg-plotdevice|backups-title}} window that shows the backup folder in the system's file manager.
backups-turn-off: Button in the {{msg-plotdevice|backups-title}} window that stops daily backups for this book. Backups already saved stay where they are.
backups-never-deleted: Important note in the {{msg-plotdevice|backups-title}} window: the app keeps every backup unless the author turns on {{msg-plotdevice|backups-cleanup}}. Keep it plain and calm, not alarming.
backups-last-title: Small heading in the {{msg-plotdevice|backups-title}} window, above when the last backup was saved and {{msg-plotdevice|backups-now}}.
backups-last: When the last backup was saved. $1: the date and time, already written in the interface's language, e.g. "5 Nov 2026, 14:30".
backups-not-yet: Shown under {{msg-plotdevice|backups-last-title}} before the first backup of this book.
backups-now: Button (and book menu item) that saves a backup of the book at once, into its backup folder; if it has none, the folder picker opens first. Keep it short.
backups-cleanup: Heading of the group of choices for removing old backups automatically. Off unless the author turns it on.
backups-cleanup-none: The default clean-up choice: nothing is ever removed.
backups-cleanup-older-before: Clean-up choice, first half: a number box follows, then {{msg-plotdevice|backups-cleanup-older-after}}. Together: "Remove backups older than [6] months". Reorder the halves' words as your language needs; the number box always sits between them.
backups-cleanup-older-after: Second half of {{msg-plotdevice|backups-cleanup-older-before}}, after the number box.
backups-cleanup-months: Screen-reader name of the number box in {{msg-plotdevice|backups-cleanup-older-before}}.
backups-cleanup-newest-before: Clean-up choice, first half: a number box follows, then {{msg-plotdevice|backups-cleanup-newest-after}}. Together: "Keep only the newest [30] backups".
backups-cleanup-newest-after: Second half of {{msg-plotdevice|backups-cleanup-newest-before}}, after the number box.
backups-cleanup-count: Screen-reader name of the number box in {{msg-plotdevice|backups-cleanup-newest-before}}.
backups-cleanup-hint: Explanation under the clean-up choices. "Back up now" is {{msg-plotdevice|backups-now}}: use the same words.
backups-note: Quiet line under the book's title in the book menu. $1: when the last backup was saved, e.g. "5 Nov 2026, 14:30".
backups-note-none: Quiet line under the book's title in the book menu, while the book has no backups.
backups-on: Notice after the author chooses a backup folder; the first backup is saved at once. $1: the folder's full path.
backup-saved: Notice after {{msg-plotdevice|backups-now}}. $1: the backup file's full path, e.g. ".../The Salt Orchard backup 2026-11-05 14.30.zip".
backups-removed: Notice after the daily backup, when the author's clean-up removed old backups. $1: how many were removed; $2: the book's title.
backup-problem-missing-folder: Notice when a backup couldn't be saved because its folder is gone (an unplugged drive, a removed sync app). Also shown in {{msg-plotdevice|backups-title}}. "Backups…" is {{msg-plotdevice|backups-menu}}.
backup-problem-no-space: Notice when the backup folder's drive is full.
backup-problem-inside-book: Notice when the chosen backup folder is inside the book's folder, which would copy backups into backups.
backup-problem-failed: Notice when a backup failed for another reason. Reassure: the book itself is untouched.
backup-offer-title: Heading of the one-time offer, shown when the author leaves a book that has some writing. $1: the book's title.
backup-offer-not-now: Button that declines the backup offer. The offer isn't shown again for this book.
backup-offer-later: Last line of the backup offer: where to find backups later. "Backups…" is {{msg-plotdevice|backups-menu}}.
restore-menu: Book menu item that opens {{msg-plotdevice|restore-title}}. The ellipsis means a window follows.
restore-title: Heading of the window listing this book's backups, newest first, to open one as a copy or replace the book with it.
restore-no-folder: Shown in {{msg-plotdevice|restore-title}} when backups were never turned on for this book.
restore-none: Shown in {{msg-plotdevice|restore-title}} when the backup folder has none.
restore-same: Shown under a chosen backup when nothing differs from the book.
restore-changed: What's different between the chosen backup and the book. $1: how many files (chapters, pages, outlines) changed since the backup.
restore-returning: What's different: files in the backup that the book no longer has; replacing brings them back. $1: how many.
restore-newer: Files added to the book after the backup was saved; they're never removed by restoring. $1: how many.
restore-copy: Button: turns the chosen backup into a book of its own beside this one, without touching this book. The safest choice.
restore-replace-ellipsis: Button: replaces the book with the chosen backup. The ellipsis means a confirmation follows ({{msg-plotdevice|restore-replace-warning}}).
restore-replace: Confirm button of {{msg-plotdevice|restore-replace-warning}}. Keep it short.
restore-replace-warning: Confirmation before replacing the book with a backup. $1: the book's title; $2: the backup's date and time, e.g. "Thursday, 5 November 2026 at 14:30". Plain, not frightening: it explains that nothing is lost.
restore-failed: Notice when restoring failed. Reassure: the book is unchanged.
restored-as-copy: Notice after {{msg-plotdevice|restore-copy}}, with a button to open it ({{msg-plotdevice|restored-open}}). $1: the new book's folder, e.g. ".../The Salt Orchard (2026-11-05 14.30)".
restored-open: Button on {{msg-plotdevice|restored-as-copy}} that opens the copy. Keep it short.
restored-replaced: Notice after replacing the book with a backup. $1: the backup's date and time.
help-about: Screen-reader name and tooltip of a small "?" that opens the guide's page about something. $1: what it explains, e.g. "Kinds of pages".
help-topic-versions: What a "?" beside the Versions window's heading explains; read as "Help: Earlier versions" ({{msg-plotdevice|help-about}}).
help-topic-outlines: What the "?" in the outline guide explains; read as "Help: Outlines" ({{msg-plotdevice|help-about}}).
help-topic-plain-text: What the "?" beside the plain-text setting explains: seeing and editing the Markdown marks themselves. Read as "Help: Plain text" ({{msg-plotdevice|help-about}}).
welcome-try-sample: Link on the start screen that opens a sample novel to explore. It's a copy kept by the app, so nothing the author does in it touches their own books.
sample-badge: Small label beside the sample book's title, in the top bar and in Recent projects. Keep it to one short word.
sample-restart: Book menu item, only in the sample book. It puts the sample back as it first was, after {{msg-plotdevice|sample-restart-confirm}}. The ellipsis means a confirmation follows.
sample-restart-confirm: Confirmation before starting the sample over. Be clear that the sample book itself is erased, and that only the author's other books are untouched; plain, not alarming.
sample-restart-action: Confirm button of {{msg-plotdevice|sample-restart-confirm}}. Keep it short.
sample-restart-failed: Notice when starting the sample over failed; nothing was changed.
